articles.title: Basilan faithful rally for peaceful BARMM polls
articles.summary: ISABELA CITY, BASILAN, Philippines — Gathering in front of the historic Sta. Isabel de Portugal Cathedral, faithful Catholics in Isabela City, Basilan lit candles as church bells tolled in unison…

blocks.text: ISABELA CITY, BASILAN, Philippines — Gathering in front of the historic Sta. Isabel de Portugal Cathedral, faithful Catholics in Isabela City, Basilan lit candles as church bells tolled in unison following the Sunday afternoon Mass, uniting in prayer on the eve of the historic Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) parliamentary elections.
The solemn gathering was led by Bishop-Prelate Leo Dalmao in response to Circular Letter No. 007, Series of 2026, issued on Saturday by the Roman Catholic Church of Isabela de Basilan.

The directive called on all Catholic parishes and quasi-parishes under the prelature to observe a simultaneous prayer, tolling of church bells, and candle lighting precisely at 6 p.m. on Sunday, Sept. 13.

The initiative highlights the local religious community’s active role in pushing for a credible, peaceful, honest, and orderly electoral exercise as the autonomous region transitions from an interim government to its first elected parliament.

Although Isabela City remains politically independent and is not part of the BARMM territory, Dalmao asked local Catholic churches to join the initiative in solidarity with the people of Basilan province and the broader Bangsamoro region.

Dalmao urged the faithful to pray for the safety of voters, election workers, security personnel, candidates, and local communities, calling for divine guidance toward genuine peace, justice, and the common good during this critical democratic transition. /cb

articles.title: Dawson College shooting survivor turned police officer reflects on friend's death 20 years on

image.caption: Former Dawson College students and survivors James Santos, centre, Meaghan Hennegan, left and Hayder Kadhim attend a ceremony commemorating the 20th anniversary of the shooting in which one person was killed and 19 others wounded, in Montreal on Friday, Sept. 11, 2026. (Christinne Muschi/The Canadia

blocks.text: Warning: The story below contains details about the moments leading up to the death of Anastasia De Sousa.
Two decades ago, James Santos saw his friend die in a shooting at a Montreal college. Now he is a Montreal police officer working for the force he says saved his life that day.
Sunday marks the 20th anniversary of the shooting.
On Sept. 13, 2006, a gunman entered Dawson College and opened fire on students in the hall. He killed 18-year-old Anastasia De Sousa and injured 19 others.

Santos, then a 17-year-old student, was having lunch with De Sousa that day. The cafeteria was packed and the two found a free table close to the entrance, he recalled in an interview with The Canadian Press.
“We were talking about our weekend and what we did and we had laughs — and then, all of a sudden, I see the shooter walk in,” he said.
When he realized the man had a real weapon, Santos dove behind some chairs. De Sousa, who couldn’t see the shooter, stood up.
“She turned around facing the shooter and basically one of the first shots was directed to my friend,” recalled Santos.
Thinking De Sousa fainted, Santos crawled over to drag her to cover.
“That's when I realized she got hit by one of the rounds near the abdomen. So I tried to console her, tell her that I was next to her and that everything will be alright,” he said.
Soon, the shooter turned his attention back to Santos. He told Santos to get up and get in front of him, essentially acting as a human shield. Santos obeyed.
“I didn't want to anger him because I believed that Anastasia was still there, and I also had other friends that were trapped,” he said.
He tried to talk the shooter down. At that moment, Santos recalled, he accepted that he would die.
“I just didn't want to take other students with me,” he said.
Her daughter was killed in the Dawson shooting. After 20 years, she still lives with the what-ifs
He fed the shooter white lies about the layout of the school, telling him one corridor led to a janitor’s closet or that another led nowhere.
When the shooter asked Santos how De Sousa was doing, Santos didn’t know what to say.
At that point, he still hoped his friend was alive. So he told the shooter that he wasn’t sure and asked him to let him get her help.

“He didn't say anything — he just loaded his magazine into a semi automatic and walked over to her, he unloaded all his 12 rounds on her, and then he came back and he told me, ‘Well, now you have nothing to worry about,’” said Santos.
Santos froze. Later, when the shooter held another student at gunpoint, Santos snapped, yelling at the shooter to leave the student be.
“I think I had enough with everything. Enough with the gunshots, the blood, the screaming of the students, just all of it," said Santos.
"The shooter didn't say anything, he just laughed.”
The shooter spared that other student. Moments later, police shot him in the leg. Santos was sure the angered gunman would shoot him. Instead, the shooter killed himself.

items: 'Why did you go to school that day?': Mother of Dawson shooting victim reflects 20 years later

blocks.text: Santos ran off. He thought it had been hours since De Sousa was killed and the ordeal began.
“I found out a little later on that it was a dozen minutes that passed by,” he said.
In 2008, then-Governor General of Canada Michaëlle Jean awarded Santos the Star of Courage for his actions that day.

Dawson College commemorated the shooting on Friday in a ceremony that brought De Sousa's family, survivors and students together in the school's Peace Garden. Loved ones remembered De Sousa's cheerful and resilient character.
During the ceremony, De Sousa's mother, Louise De Sousa, called on the federal government to tighten gun control laws.
Santos said the journey to becoming an officer was a challenging one, as he worked over years to overcome the trauma.
Talking about the events of that day two decades later, Santos seems calm, his voice never wavering.
“I have all the details in my mind. I recall everything, but I don't put myself into it. I'm looking at it as a third person,” he said.
That wasn’t always the case, he said.
“Initially, saying it the first couple of times was extremely, extremely, extremely hard. There's really no words to place it, just because you pretty much relive every second of it,” he said.

items: 'Why did I make it?': Survivors of Dawson shooting on compassion, finding purpose

blocks.text: Nonetheless, as he tells the story, little details come up. The way De Sousa had wanted to go out for lunch, but Santos instead opted to eat at the cafeteria. The fact that she sat with her back to the door and couldn’t see the shooter coming in.
Santos said he fixated on some of these details after graduating from Dawson, filled with survivor’s guilt.
“What if I had given her the [other] chair?" he asked.
"It just goes down that spiral that it's extremely hard to get out because you could think of anything, but it'll never change what actually happened."
He had considered a career in law enforcement before the event of 2006, and he said his experience during the shooting pushed him to want to join the Montreal police.
“I wanted to give back to the community that gave me another chance, right? The police [officers] gave me another chance at life.”

The path to get there wasn’t easy. Santos had vivid nightmares and panic attacks, and he knew he would have to address his trauma if he wanted to work as a police officer. He turned to therapy and set small goals, like watching an action movie, or one with a lot of shooting, until he could get through it calmly.
Then he joined the army. Training was a challenge, he said.
“The smell of gunpowder would bring me right back to the event of Dawson,” he said.
After about a decade in the military, Santos got into the police academy. He then worked for a year in a town outside of Montreal before joining the Montreal force in 2018.

“As a police officer, you never know what calls you're getting. [If] I get a call, I'm not going to be having anxiety or sweating or anything, because of all the little things I did prior to get myself to where I am today,” he said.

articles.title: Trump downplays AI risks after dire expert warnings and calls to slow development down
articles.summary: The US President said "negative forces" were airing concerns about "things that won't happen".

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has downplayed risks posed by artificial intelligence following days of dire warnings by experts.
"You have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen," Trump said during a visit to Ireland.
One of the warnings came from a former Anthropic researcher who said "there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future" if the current pace of development continued.

On Saturday, top industry bosses agreed and called for a slow-down. Trump did not directly address the idea, but said: "We're leading China on AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins."
Trump spoke on the same day AI researcher Jacob Coxon - who quit Anthropic a few days ago - told the BBC staff who were developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity.
Coxon – who has also worked at OpenAI – welcomed the idea of a slowdown but said it would need to be co-ordinated with China.

On Saturday, Elon Musk, owner of xAI, and Sam Altman of OpenAI, backed a warning from the head of Anthropic Dario Amodei that the pace of development should be slowed "to reduce the risk that something goes seriously wrong".
The Anthropic CEO said any slowdown would have to be limited to avoid allowing China to pull ahead.
The issues surrounding AI have prompted fierce debate - and present a dilemma for many world leaders.
On one hand, the sector is seen as huge opportunity to boost economic growth and a way to improve outdated digital systems and ways of working.
But there have also been a number of incidents where AI appears to have gone seriously wrong.
In August OpenAI said it had slowed down training some of its most advanced AI models to improve security.
The ChatGPT-maker said it was adding new measures after its AI agents bypassed safeguards and hacked the tech start-up Hugging Face.
And the same month it was disclosed two of the world's most powerful AI tools created fake human profiles to try and trick people in attempted cyber-attacks.

The UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) said in the most serious case, Anthropic's Mythos AI tried to gain access to a service by sending private messages, having set up fake accounts mimicking real people - then hid the evidence.

articles.title: First ministers at Celtic summit to affirm right to seek independence from the UK
articles.summary:
Call for ‘constitutional change in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland’ likely to challenge Burnham’s devolution agenda

The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland are…

blocks.text: The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland are meeting to affirm their nations’ right to seek independence from the UK, as part of a summit that is likely to challenge Andy Burnham’s devolution agenda.

Plaid Cymru leader Rhun ap Iorwerth, Scottish National party leader John Swinney and Sinn Féin vice president Michelle O’Neill are expected to sign a memorandum of understanding at a landmark conference in Cardiff on Monday, calling on Westminster “to prepare, plan and facilitate constitutional change in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland”.

The three are meeting in their capacity as party leaders, rather than as officials in their respective governments, alongside Sinn Féin president and leader of the opposition in Ireland, Mary Lou McDonald. They will also discuss Europe, international cooperation, the economy and energy issues.
Plaid Cymru’s victory in May’s Senedd elections ushered in a new era for the Celtic independence movements: for the first time, separatist parties are now in government in all three nations.

While Burnham has made much of his support for regional devolution of power and resources in England since becoming prime minister in July, his approach to the devolved administrations in Belfast, Cardiff and Edinburgh is less clear.
Last week, Burnham wrote to Swinney to reiterate that a repeat of 2014’s Scottish independence referendum remains “off limits”, after apparently misspeaking during prime minister’s questions.

Donald Trump also weighed in on a potential break-up of the UK during a weekend visit to Ireland, telling reporters at a media conference with the taoiseach, Micheál Martin, that he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and the unionist power-sharing members of the Northern Ireland executive.

Asked about the diplomatic backlash this caused, Trump said on Sunday: “I love my comments.” Shortly after doubling down on his comments on Irish unity the US president said he will save his opinion on Scottish independence for “another day”.

Ap Iorwerth told the Guardian this week that while he has been encouraged by warm initial discussions with Burnham – a stark contrast to interactions with his predecessor, Keir Starmer – he was wary about the new prime minister being captured by a consensus Westminster view against relinquishing further powers.
A Plaid Cymru source called Monday’s summit an opportunity for “a new partnership between our nations”.

“Following the historic Senedd election in Wales and the changing political landscape across these islands, there is a strong case for practical political cooperation on areas including energy, the economy and our relationship with Europe, as well as on the wider political and constitutional questions facing our nations and on the right to self-determination.
“Our parties have much to gain from working together, as partners and as equals, where we share common interests and where cooperation can improve the lives of the people we represent,” they added.

Speaking before his visit to Cardiff on Monday, Swinney said: “We are at a pivotal moment of constitutional change, and our parties share the common belief that our interests will never be served by Westminster, and that the people of our respective nations must have a meaningful say over their future.

“This discussion comes the week after the prime minister accepted that a referendum should take place when there is majority support for independence in Scotland. That acknowledgment that the people of Scotland can and should determine their own constitutional future is long overdue.”

Latest polling suggests 47% of Scottish voters would opt for independence in a referendum held tomorrow, along with 36% in Northern Ireland and 32% in Wales. Support for independence in Scotland has hovered between 45% – 50% since the 2014 referendum, while data trends suggest it is rising in Wales and Northern Ireland.

articles.title: Russia struck train near Poland border shortly after Boris Johnson and top European officials passed through
articles.summary: The former UK PM said "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning".

blocks.text: A Russian strike has hit a train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and other top European officials had passed through.
No casualties were reported after the Russian strike, which hit the train's engine.
Johnson and some of Europe's most senior security advisers, including the UK's Jonathan Powell, had passed along the same line on their way back from a conference in the capital, Kyiv.

Russia said Sunday it struck "railway infrastructure" in western Ukraine, but the former PM said "I don't know what warped logic drove Putin to blow up a stationary Ukrainian locomotive on the Polish border this morning" and asked "When are we going to give them the air defences they need?"
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a Russian drone had struck 800m from Polish border.
Russia has in recent months carried out a number of deadly attacks targeting Ukraine's trains, railway depots and other transport facilities.
Earlier this month, six employees of the state railway company Ukrzaliznytsia were killed after a depot was hit in Kyiv.
This week, a female conductor died in a Russian drone attack on a passenger train in southern Ukraine.
In January, President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned as "terrorism" a Russian strike on a crowded passenger train in the north-eastern Kharkiv region that left five people dead.

The Russian attacks have significantly damaged Ukraine's vast train network - the main mode of transportation for millions of Ukrainians as all air travel has been suspended since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

articles.title: Wisconsin congressman swims to safety after plane makes emergency landing in lake
articles.summary:
Republican gubernatorial candidate Tom Tiffany and pilot swim to safety after plane made emergency landing in lake

A Republican congressman said he had to swim to safety after a plane he was…

blocks.text: A Republican congressman said he had to swim to safety after a plane he was traveling in made an emergency landing in a lake late Saturday.

Representative Tom Tiffany says he was returning from the La Crosse county Lincoln Day Dinner when the light aircraft lost power as it approached Wausau downtown airport. The pilot made an emergency landing in Lake Wausau. They both ended up in the water and swam to safety.
“After landing, we called 911. As the plane began to submerge, we exited the aircraft and swam to a shallow area, where we waited until emergency responders reached us by boat,” he wrote on X.
Emergency responders got both Tiffany and the pilot to a nearby hospital, where they were treated for minor injuries.
Tiffany is running for governor on the Republican ticket in Wisconsin and has been endorsed by Donald Trump.
The plane Tiffany was traveling in was a single-engine, four-seat Bonanza aircraft.

articles.title: ‘Biased impeach vote likely for absent senator-judges’
articles.summary: Senator-judges who missed the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte might end up voting based solely on political persuasion or alliances, Sen. Panfilo Lacson warned yesterday,…

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate opens impeachment court to public, but limits use of devices Senators start the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate in Pasay, Metro Manila on July 6, 2026.
Aaron Favila, pool via AFP

MANILA, Philippines — Senator-judges who missed the impeachment proceedings against Vice President Sara Duterte might end up voting based solely on political persuasion or alliances, Sen. Panfilo Lacson warned yesterday, questioning how absent members can make an informed decision to convict or acquit the impeached official.
In an interview over radio dzBB, Lacson voiced concerns that colleagues who failed to hear testimony and observe witness demeanor throughout the trial could compromise fairness.
“How can they decide now? They will just rely on their political persuasion or political alliance,” he said.

Lacson raised the issue as the impeachment court prepares to consult with four amici curiae (friends of the court): retired chief justices Artemio Panganiban, Reynato Puno and Hilario Davide Jr., and retired Supreme Court associate justice Adolfo Azcuna, regarding the required voting threshold for conviction.
The legal experts were invited after presiding officer Francis Escudero consulted the prosecution and defense panels.
Senator-judges are expected to vote on Sen. Erwin Tulfo’s motion for reconsideration regarding the 16-vote, or two-thirds threshold previously ruled on by Escudero.
Lacson cautioned the Senate against intervening in the petitions of detained Senators Rodante Marcoleta and Jinggoy Estrada to participate in the trial.
Marcoleta has written to Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian and Escudero seeking permission to vote, while Estrada’s bid to attend was rejected by the Sandiganbayan in July.
Bato, Loren
Asked about Sen. Ronald dela Rosa, Lacson distinguished between members who never took the oath as judges and those who did but missed proceedings.
Dela Rosa has been in hiding following the issuance of an arrest warrant against him by the International Criminal Court and after fleeing the Senate compound following a shooting incident on May 13.

Meanwhile, Sen. Loren Legarda has been abroad for several weeks now amid personal health issues and plunder allegations over P10.44 billion in incomplete solar energy projects awarded to her son, Batangas Rep. Leandro Leviste.
Lacson said Legarda has reached out to colleagues for moral support.

articles.title: AMLC to confirm P6.7 billion bank transactions of VP, Mans?
articles.summary: The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) is expected to present to the Senate impeachment court today its report on the P6.7 billion in transactions linked to the bank accounts of Vice President Sara…

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte arrives before the start of the impeachment trial at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay, Metro Manila on July 7, 2026.
Noel Celis, pool / AFP

MANILA, Philippines — The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) is expected to present to the Senate impeachment court today its report on the P6.7 billion in transactions linked to the bank accounts of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio under Article II of the impeachment, on unexplained wealth.

The AMLC report was previously discussed during House proceedings on Duterte’s impeachment, with the figures cited including P6.7 billion in aggregate transactions and P4.4 billion in inflows involving the couple.

The figure represents aggregated transactions over the years and is not by itself equivalent to the couple’s net worth, making the underlying bank records important to establishing what the transactions actually represent.
Of the P6.7 billion, “inflows” amounted to P4.4 billion, while “outflows” totaled P1.5 billion.

Prosecutors have since obtained bank and tax records through subpoenas issued by the Senate impeachment court, giving them access to financial documents that were not available during the earlier House inquiry.

Additionally, the prosecution has lined up retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang, ombudsman records division officer-in-charge Karen Batu and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) company registration and monitoring department director Gerardo del Rosario among its witnesses today.
Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno will be the prosecutor in charge of Article II.

Cabotaje-Tang is expected to testify on principles governing public accountability and integrity in public office, including mechanisms for addressing undisclosed or unexplained wealth and prohibited business interests.

Batu will testify on Duterte’s statement of assets, liabilities and net worth in the custody of the Office of the Ombudsman, while Del Rosario is expected to identify and authenticate SEC records involving companies and business interests linked to Duterte and Carpio.
Article II accuses Duterte of betrayal of public trust for allegedly accumulating wealth disproportionate to her lawful income and failing to fully and truthfully disclose her assets and liabilities.

Earlier, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon, one of the House prosecutors who will be helping Diokno in Article II, said the prosecution was completing preparations for both its documentary and testimonial evidence.
The prosecution is preparing more than 1,800 bank, tax and other financial documents for Article II, including records involving Duterte, Carpio and companies linked to them.
Ridon had described bank and Bureau of Internal Revenue records obtained by the prosecution as the “last important pillar” of its evidence on Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth.

Prosecutors plan to examine the financial records alongside Duterte’s SALNs and information from the AMLC to determine whether her assets and financial transactions can be reconciled with her declared wealth and legitimate sources of income.
The prosecution has also served Duterte with 104 requests for admission involving subpoenaed bank records and the ownership of accounts identified in them.
Commenting on the impeachment case and criminal complaint for grave threats filed at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court, Ridon said Duterte only has herself to blame.

As far as Ridon is concerned, Duterte’s open threat to have President Marcos, First Lady Liza Marcos and former speaker Martin Romualdez killed was the original sin that resulted in her cases today, adding she should stop insinuating political motivations for her problems.

articles.title: House plenary debates on 2027 budget begin this week
articles.summary: Plenary deliberations on the P7.2-trillion national budget will start this week at the House of Representatives, as lawmakers try to finish the government’s spending bill before the…

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Plenary deliberations on the P7.2-trillion national budget will start this week at the House of Representatives, as lawmakers try to finish the government’s spending bill before the congressional recess next month and until after the Undas break.
Sponsorship and plenary debates on the 2027 General Appropriations Bill (GAB) will start Tuesday and are expected to be finished on Sept. 25.

The Development Budget Coordination Committee led by the Department of Budget and Management and Department of Finance, in coordination with the Department of Economy, Planning and Development, Office of the President and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas submitted the 2027 National Expenditure Plan to the House last Aug. 11.

Under the House’s schedule of activities, second reading of the 2027 GAB is slated on Oct. 6 to be followed by the third reading on Oct. 9, after which it will be transmitted to the Senate on the same day.

House appropriations committee chair Mikaela Suansing and Speaker Faustino Dy III said the chamber is on track with its timeline in passing the 2027 GAB, with Dy assuring taxpayers that they will scrutinize every centavo in the budget for 2027 to ensure public funds are properly allocated.

Speaking at a press briefing over the weekend in a public consultation in South Cotabato, Dy said the national budget is currently the most important measure being tackled by the House because of its direct impact on communities and families across the country.
DepEd budget augmentation

Sibling Reps. Migz and Luigi Villafuerte of the 5th and 2nd districts of Camarines Sur, respectively, are pushing for the augmentation of the Department of Education’s P975.9-billion budget for 2027 by adding P12 billion more for the career growth program of teachers and school heads.
In separate statements, they underscored the need for this year’s promotion of more than 5,000 public school teachers and school heads in the province alone.

articles.summary: Several Indian firms committed to expand their operations in the Philippines, including on agricultural technology, health care and digital infrastructure during their meeting with President Marcos…

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. arrives at New Delhi, India on September 12, 2026 to attend the 18th BRICS Summit where he will represent the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
Photo / Presidential Communications Office

MANILA, Philippines — Several Indian firms committed to expand their operations in the Philippines, including on agricultural technology, health care and digital infrastructure during their meeting with President Marcos in New Delhi, India on Saturday.

In a statement yesterday, the Presidential Communications Office (PCO) said Marcos met with iSON Group, a New Delhi-based conglomerate with businesses in agrotechnology, health care, telecommunications, information technology, renewable energy, business process outsourcing (BPO) and insurance.
According to Trade Secretary Cristina Roque, iSON Group discussed expansion plans in three key areas: agricultural technology, health care, and BPO and digital infrastructure.
The group has committed $75 million in new and scaled-up investments in the Philippines, which is expected to generate around 2,000 jobs, PCO said.
The investments include a proposed $50-million agro-solar project, health care and 24/7 teleconsultation services, and a $10-million expansion in BPO and global delivery centers.?
Roque said the proposed teleconsultation service could help address health care access challenges in remote communities.
The proposed service would cost around P65 per month and allow patients to consult doctors at any time, subject to the company’s final implementation plans.?
“This is very helpful for us, especially in areas where access to doctors and health care facilities remains limited,” Roque said.??

With more than 25,000 employees and operations in around 35 countries, iSON Group through its digital infrastructure arm iSON Tower Ltd. Inc., has operated in the Philippines since 2021 under the Department of Information and Communications Technology’s Common Tower Policy.
The company has deployed around $65 million to build 450 telecommunications towers serving approximately 600 tenants across Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.

Marcos also met with NPCI International Ltd. to advance cooperation on digital payments, including a partnership with LandBank to explore the adoption in the Philippines of a payment system based on India’s Unified Payments Interface.
The initiative could make government payments more efficient, improve interoperability of QR-based payments, and facilitate faster cross-border transactions.

The President likewise met with executives of GMR Group and representatives of Cavitex Holdings Inc. to advance the development of the Sangley Point International Airport project – a world-class, multi-runway aviation hub that will help decongest the Ninoy Aquino International Airport.

Marcos also led an executive roundtable discussion with executives of Cognizant, VVDN Technologies, Hinduja Group and HCLTech, which already have operations or a presence in the Philippines.?Roque said the four companies indicated plans to expand in digitalization, AI, telecommunications and other technology-driven industries.??
Also present during the meetings were Finance Secretary Frederick Go, Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda and other senior officials from the Philippine government.?
Marcos was in India to attend the 18th BRICS Summit on Sunday in his capacity as this year’s chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
He was also expected to hold a bilateral meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

articles.title: Gibo to reserve force: Protect Philippines land, maritime domain
articles.summary: Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has called on the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Reserve Force to help protect the country’s maritime domain.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.
Department of National Defense - Philippines / Facebook page
MANILA, Philippines — Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has called on the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Reserve Force to help protect the country’s maritime domain.

Teodoro made the call during the culmination of the 47th AFP National Reservist Week at Camp Aguinaldo on Saturday as he highlighted the Reserve Force’s role in addressing gaps in the AFP’s active duty force structure through “force and mission replication and support,” including “functional replication, and substitution, if necessary, of operating units.”

He asked the Reserve Force to pursue activities along the Pacific Ocean boundary and areas leading to the Pacific Ocean, particularly in coastal and island provinces, where the country faces vulnerabilities in its eastern seaboard.

“Our vulnerability is in the eastern seaboard. I would like the Reserve Commands to pursue activities on our Pacific Ocean boundary and or areas leading to the Pacific Ocean. That is a huge gap,” Teodoro said.

As a maritime and archipelagic country, he said the Philippines must control its territorial land domain, baseline areas from which its maritime entitlements are drawn, its exclusive economic zone (EEZ), and other areas under its jurisdiction, including its extended continental shelves.

He emphasized the country’s responsibility to help secure supply chains and protect Filipino seafarers, whom he identified as the number one nationality victimized by piracy and other untoward activities due to world and ethnic conflicts elsewhere.
He identified three major threats confronting the country according to their imminence: natural calamities and disasters, internal and external security threats, and actual conflict.

For internal and external security threats, he emphasized deterrence as the country’s prime objective, requiring increased posture through infrastructure, capabilities, force size, and activities conducted singly, bilaterally, or multilaterally to demonstrate the ability to resist threats.

Teodoro emphasized the need for continued modernization, infrastructure build-up, enhancing community survivability, and internal hardening against malign foreign influence and disinformation, noting the reality of cognitive warfare and changing narratives.

articles.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the…

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa attends the Senate session on Monday, May 11, 2026, hours before being placed under Senate protective custody amid reports of an alleged ICC arrest warrant.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.
Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.?

“One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday.
He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed.

“If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said.
He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage.

“The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said.
The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa.
Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war.
Dela Rosa left the Senate with Sen. Robinhood Padilla early on May 14.
A DOJ special prosecutor panel later concluded that the Senate had not been under attack and that the actions of then-acting Senate sergeant-at-arms Mao Aplasca were not justified.
Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla dismissed Aplasca on June 25 for grave misconduct and gross neglect of duty over the shooting incident.?
The ombudsman is expected to determine whether sufficient evidence exists to bring charges before the courts.

articles.title: ICC sets 3rd status conference on Duterte case
articles.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will hold on Wednesday the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
This photograph taken on March 14, 2025 shows the International Criminal Court (ICC) in The Hague.
AFP / Nicolas Tucat

MANILA, Philippines — The International Criminal Court (ICC) Trial Chamber III will hold on Wednesday the third status conference on the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte.
The conference, scheduled to start 10:30 a.m. in The Hague (4:30 p.m. in Manila), will be livestreamed online with a 30-minute delay.

It will tackle details of the prosecution’s case, including its list of witnesses and evidence, the number of hours to be given to the prosecutor, the ongoing disclosure to the defense and other possible incidents to be added in the case.
The parties will also discuss the trial schedule, which will start on Nov. 30, including the proposal to have “blocks of hearings with breaks.”
It remains unclear if Duterte will be present as he was previously allowed to skip the pre-trial proceedings.

But during the last status conference on June 23, presiding judge Joanna Korner said they expect Duterte to attend the September status conference “unless there’s some medical issue” that would prevent him from doing so.
Duterte has never appeared in person before ICC judges.
He was last seen by the public on March 14, 2025, when he appeared via video link during his initial appearance hearing before the ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I.
His family and lawyers regularly visit him in his detention facility in The Hague.

articles.title: PGH to submit Romualdez’s medical report to Sandiganbayan
articles.summary: The Philippine General Hospital (PGH) is set to submit its medical report on former House speaker and Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez to the Sandiganbayan.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am

Bureau of Jail Management and Penology officers escort an ambulance reportedly carrying former speaker Martin Romualdez as the convoy arrives at the Philippine General Hospital in Manila on September 12, 2026.
Noel Pabalate
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine General Hospital (PGH) is set to submit its medical report on former House speaker and Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez to the Sandiganbayan.
The medical report will determine whether Romualdez will still need hospital confinement. The recommendation was expected to be submitted yesterday at 5 p.m.
PGH spokesperson Dr. Jonas del Rosario said they were still finishing medical tests on the lawmaker, as of yesterday morning.
Del Rosario said they were in the last stage of completion of the medical exam, as of 1 p.m. yesterday.
The doctor said that a group of specialists would discuss the specific findings on Romualdez’s medical test results.

As ordered by the Sandiganbayan Third Division, Romualdez was transferred from Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan to PGH to undergo independent medical and diagnostic tests to determine if there is justification for his request for continued hospital detention.

Dr. Gerardo Legaspi, director of UP-PGH, is set to testify before the Sandiganbayan tomorrow on the hospital’s findings and recommendation. He has also been directed to submit a daily medical report on Romualdez’s condition.
The first cousin of President Marcos will stay in PGH until the Sandiganbayan orders his transfer to the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas.
Romualdez is facing plunder charges for allegedly receiving P7.4 billion in kickbacks from promised government projects from 2022 to 2025.
‘Main plunderers’
Both Romualdez and fugitive former congressman Zaldy Co should be held liable as “main plunderers” for squandering P7.4 billion worth of public funds, Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla said.

His office filed plunder charges against Romualdez, Co, and Romualdez’s household staff Joselyn Serenio and foreign exchange executive Felicito Guevarra over alleged deliveries of part of the funds, as well as establishing dummy companies to be able to buy properties.

Asked whether Romualdez or Co should be tagged as the “main plunderer” based on jurisprudence, Remulla maintained both of them should be called such because they amassed P7.4 billion, far greater than the P50 million threshold to press plunder cases.
Remulla believes the Supreme Court will “revisit” the “main plunderer doctrine.”
“I am sure of it because that kind of thinking must not be entertained because that is meant to protect plunderers, not to convict them.”
Meanwhile, Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said it would be “prudent for us to see what he wants to say if ever he is willing to do so,” referring to Co.

“Former speaker Martin (Romualdez) may not have reached his quota if Zaldy (Co) did not move. In our eyes, they are both guilty of this plunder charge,” Clavano said in a recent interview over ANC. — Ghio Ong

articles.title: Cayetanos back from Singapore
articles.summary: Senators Alan Peter and Pia Cayetano returned to the country on Saturday night following a brief trip to Singapore that drew public scrutiny.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Senators Alan Peter and Pia Cayetano arrive from Singapore at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport on Saturday night.
MANILA, Philippines — Senators Alan Peter and Pia Cayetano returned to the country on Saturday night following a brief trip to Singapore that drew public scrutiny.
Hours after arriving in Manila, Alan took to Facebook Live to accuse Sen. Panfilo Lacson of unjustly targeting his family and their bailiwick.

“Perhaps we didn’t think it would be this severe, that there would be this much hardships, this much accusations, that is being done by Sen. Lacson. I don’t know what to call it anymore, but the persecution is not only aimed at me and my family, but to our beloved city of Taguig. I leave this to God,” he said.

Lacson, in recent weeks, has continuously linked Alan to anomalous infrastructure projects in Taguig, including an alleged reclamation of Laguna de Bay. The Office of the Ombudsman is currently investigating the matter.
The National Bureau of Investigation is also looking at Alan’s involvement in alleged corruption during the 2019 Southeast Asian Games, which the Philippines hosted.
The younger Cayetano sibling dismissed controversies surrounding his overseas travel amid the ongoing probe, defending it as a “routine quiet short trip” meant for rest.
He emphasized that the Bureau of Immigration and the ombudsman found no legal impediment to his departure.
Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri previously said Alan’s trip was for health reasons.
Pia, on the other hand, said she went to Singapore to support the Philippine National Padel Team as it prepared for the Asian Games in Japan.
The Cayetano siblings left Manila for Singapore on the evening of Sept. 9.

articles.title: Speed upidentification of ferry fire victims – President Marcos
articles.summary: President Marcos has ordered government agencies to mobilize specialists and resources to expedite the identification and transport of victims of the ferry fire in Coron, Palawan.

blocks.text: September 14, 2026 | 12:00am

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) says joint authorities reported an initial count of 30 cadavers recovered on board MV June Aster on September 11, 2026, following the declaration of fire out and subsequent safety assessment.

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has ordered government agencies to mobilize specialists and resources to expedite the identification and transport of victims of the ferry fire in Coron, Palawan.
Citing official reports, Cabinet Secretary Benhur Abalos said only five of the 76 confirmed fatalities in a fire involving the MV June Aster had been identified.
Abalos led a meeting with national government agencies and local officials in Coron yesterday on the directive of the President, who was in New Delhi, India for the 18th BRICS Summit.
“The President’s order is to deliver all help needed. We must mobilize the specialists, resources and funding needed to identify the victims as quickly and accurately as possible,” Abalos said.

Forensic personnel are extracting molar teeth from the remains because dental tissue may still provide DNA samples that can be used for identification, according to Abalos, citing the Philippine National Police Forensics Unit.
The PNP Forensics Unit requested augmentation of forensic odontologists from national headquarters, as only one specialist was available to perform the extraction procedure.
Volunteer dentists have since begun assisting the Crime Laboratory.

Abalos said he called PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. to ensure that agencies would get the much-needed support to expedite the identification and transport of the specimens to PNP headquarters in Quezon City.
A disaster victim identification team from Camp Crame arrived in Palawan on Saturday, said Lt. Col. Richard Allan Mangalip, commander of the PNP Regional Forensic Unit Mimaropa.
He said that based on their initial assessment of the cadavers, “most were already in charred conditions,” but they would do their best to collect DNA samples.
According to an ABS-CBN report, the local government of Coron dug a mass grave at the San Nicolas Public Cemetery to temporarily bury unidentified victims of the passenger and cargo ship.
As of Saturday evening, the PCG reported that the death toll was at 76 while the number of survivors remained at 43, and the number of missing people went down to 13.
Dindo Macalinao, human resources generalist of Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc., said he has no information as to the whereabouts of the captain of June Aster, identified as Roel Sarmiento.

The PCG said that while there continues to be no sign of oil sheen or an oil spill, the June Aster would eventually be removed from its location where it had run aground after the fire last Wednesday evening. — Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: In historic first, Bangsamoro people go to polls to choose a new parliament
articles.summary: After decades of armed struggle and years of delays, the conduct of the election is a success in itself

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY, Philippines – The Bangsamoro people are finally set to elect their parliament on Monday, September 14, after decades of armed struggle and historical injustices, years of painstaking negotiations with the Philippine government, and repeated electoral delays.

Polls open as early as 5 am for senior citizens, pregnant women, and persons with disabilities, with the early voting hours lasting until 7 am — the start of regular voting hours. Polls close at 7 pm.
More than two million voters are expected to cast their ballots at their local precincts.

As the elections drew near, tensions had heightened between security forces and members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF). Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) Interim Chief Abdulraof Macacua was ambushed a month before election day. Nearly 12,000 troops and militiamen have since been deployed.

In Cotabato City, Bangsamoro’s regional center, candidates’ and parties’ tarpaulins decorated the sides of roads and were displayed in front of houses and stores. In this city, rival political parties United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) and Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP) held their miting de avance at venues close to each other on Saturday, September 12, the last day of the campaign.
Despite the warning signs, the elections remain an endeavor of hope.
“Something hopeful is happening in the Philippines” was how civil society groups put it. “And it’s happening in the BARMM.”

blocks.caption: CAMP. Government housing for former rebels seen in Camp Darapanan, one of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front’s biggest strongholds. Photo by Martin San Diego/Rappler

blocks.text: It’s a hopeful election not only because it marks a historic moment for the Bangsamoro people but because it paves the way for a government designed differently from the one the rest of the country has been used to.

In this parliamentary government, political parties are supposed to take center stage instead of personalities. Some of these parties came from the rebel groups that led the struggle for self-governance.
Marginalized sectors such as non-Moro indigenous peoples, women, and youth get representation with a definite number of seats allotted to them.

But this design is often challenged by realities on the ground. Political science professors Yasmira Moner and Aries Arugay offered a somber assessment in their analysis for ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute’s Fulcrum: “Peace settlements rarely spawn instantaneous, mature, inclusive, and democratic arrangements.”
Fractures within the MILF have led some members to run under a different party, BFP. Most notably, MILF’s former military chief, Macacua, is chairman of the BFP.

Factions of the Moro National Liberation Front have also formed different parties, including Nur Misuari’s Mahardika Party and Muslimin Sema’s Bangsamoro Party. Then, there’s the BARMM Grand Coalition, which includes traditional political families in Mindanao such as the Adiongs and Mangudadatus.
A single party may find it difficult to dominate the parliament.

“‘Yung iba rin, ganito rin ang expectation nila, na baka nga mahihirapan magkaroon ng single party majority after the election,“ UBJP spokesperson Mojahirin Ali told reporters on Friday, September 11. “So, we will be expecting a coalition among parties to form a government.”
(The others share the same expectation that we may have a hard time having a single-party majority after the elections.)
Meanwhile, Macacua’s BFP offers to unite other parties and sectors.
“Bangsamoro Federalist Party is a unifier party na walang kinikilala, Muslim man, Lumad man, Christian man, kailangan nating pagsilbihan lahat,” Macacua said during BFP’s grand rally on Saturday.
(Bangsamoro Federalist Party is a unifier party that doesn’t discriminate; whether you’re a Muslim, Lumad, or Christian, we will serve you all.)

blocks.caption: The dynasties, elites, and parties competing for power in BARMM

blocks.text: “Winning the peace is one thing, governing BARMM’s post-conflict environment is a totally different matter,” Moner and Arugay wrote.

Some questions may arise in the aftermath of the election: Which factions will command a majority in the 80-member parliament? What will be the priorities of the new government? Will decommissioning resume soon?
And the most immediate: Who will be the next chief minister?

blocks.caption: GROUND ZERO. Sittie Norjannah Gambao and her mother, displaced residents of Marawi City, look inside their former home in the city. Photo by Martin San Diego/Rappler

blocks.text: The answer to that will come a little later, when the parliament assumes office on October 30 and eventually holds its first session.

In the meantime, conducting a peaceful and credible election is the primary objective of many stakeholders who have come down south for this historic event. President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has promised as much.
The answers to all the other questions are for the new Bangsamoro government to provide. The elected parliament will have until June 2031 to deliver progress and lasting peace in the region.

blocks.caption: For Moros, the price of peace is life

articles.title: Who better to defend Reform’s latest millions than Honest Bob Jenrick? | John Crace
articles.summary:
The man who once helped Richard ‘Dirty’ Desmond save a load of tax was wheeled out to face Laura Kuenssberg

You wait years for one party donation of £36m and then

blocks.text: You wait years for one party donation of £36m and then two come along at once. Reform can hardly believe its luck. All hail the crypto billionaires. Tacky pale turquoise suits all round. And Nigel Farage won’t have to worry about spending any of his own money – if you can call the £5m freebie his own money – on his security. Nor do those champagne and oyster lunches to discuss loose change donations of £500k from people living overseas pay for themselves. From now on Reform won’t need to bother getting out of bed for anything less than eight figures.

Fair to say that if it had been Labour or the Tories trousering £72m from Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo then Reform would be on full outrage rampage. How the political system was rigged against it and how the two main parties are hotwired cash machines. In bed with the super-rich. But since the money is heading towards its own bank account, everyone in the party is totally chilled. This is just the way life ought to be. Who wouldn’t want a country where two billionaires can attempt to buy the democratic process?

So it was a joy to find that Reform had sent out Robert Jenrick to gloat about its unexpected cash windfall on the Laura Kuenssberg show. Who better to speak about the party’s incorruptibility than the man, who as a junior minister in the Tory government, unlawfully overruled the government’s own planning inspector and just happened to save the Tory donor cum pornographer, Richard “Dirty” Desmond, the best part of £45m in tax. And what did the Tories get in return? A gift of about £12k. You’d have hoped the lesson Honest Bob had learned from that was not to sell his soul – if he has one – so cheaply.

“Everything was totally above board,” he insisted. Though forgive us all for asking the question. Reform is currently the subject of at least two – or is it three? it’s so easy to lose count – police investigations into alleged financial wrongdoing, and the party has acquired a reputation for being at the sleazier end of British politics. A place where Dicky Tice shuffles money from Posh George into and out of his accounts and Nige is so blase he can’t even be bothered to listen when two potential donors talk at length on how they are planning to break the law. Remarkable stuff. Nige can even not listen while maintaining a conversation.

Laura did suggest that Reform might have to give some of the money back if the government were to retrospectively implement the findings of the Rycroft review into party funding. But Honest Bob wasn’t having any of it. There was no way he would be handing back a penny. Finders keepers. Possession nine-tenths of the law. You’d be amazed how Reform can make money disappear when it feels like it. Though, of course, everything would be done in a totally legitimate way.

What we all had to understand was that this was a huge vote of confidence in Reform. Far from being an indication that the party’s funding had become exponentially more murky, this was proof that it was being totally transparent. Think of it this way. When he had been a Conservative MP, Honest Bob had been more than happy for his party to shower peerages on donors. Some only had to hand over less than £100k to end up in the Lords. But Delo and Harborne weren’t asking for anything like that. All they wanted was for the laws around crypto currencies to be relaxed a little. Where was the conflict of interest in that?
after newsletter promotion

Ben and Christopher were just regular guys who just happened to be billionaires. And yes, it was unfortunate that Ben had been convicted in the US for failing to comply with anti-money-laundering legislation – somehow the fact he had been pardoned by Donald Trump made him sound doubly guilty – but this had just been an oversight. He was a very busy man and it had been the sort of mistake anyone could make.

“They are both just patriots,” Honest Bob continued. So patriotic that Delo had spent much of the last few years based in Hong Kong while Harborne lived in Thailand. We should try to feel their pain. They were both just run-of-the-mill billionaires who happened to have been priced out of Mayfair. Rather than indulge in the politics of envy, we should applaud them for their philanthropy. Two guys just trying to make a difference. Making Britain better.

Now and again, Honest Bob found himself getting a little confused. For example, when he came to think about it, Delo and Harborne giving £72m from their crypto empires was much the same as tens of thousands of ordinary workers donating to Labour through their union subscriptions. Because what Ben and Chris wanted most was for the income tax threshold to be raised to £15k. That £500 they would get back could make the difference between them remaining tax exiles and returning to this country.

The money would be spent on the professionalisation of Reform. When all welfare payments – those that were left – would be paid in crypto. When Reform would rise above the ashes of sleaze. When all bus sites and billboards would be covered with adverts for Reform. When all TV stations promoted Reform without question. It wasn’t enough to have GB News doing that for nothing. There would be no rest until the BBC had also been captured. Make no mistake. This £72m was only the start.

articles.title: Pregnant woman among more than 10 killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
articles.summary:
Woman’s family says she died of injuries after being shot in the head while sitting inside a tent near Khan Younis

A pregnant Palestinian woman died on Saturday from injuries sustained after…
articles.byline: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem and Seham Tantesh in Gaza

blocks.text: A pregnant Palestinian woman died on Saturday from injuries sustained after being shot in the head by Israeli forces south of Khan Younis, according to her family and medical workers, as strikes across Gaza killed at least 10 people in 48 hours.

The woman, named as Iman Shalouf, 27, who was nearly eight months pregnant, was sitting inside her family’s tent in the al-Mawasi area when Israeli gunfire struck her, according to paramedics and witnesses.

‘‘We heard the sound of gunfire while I was praying,’’ Wathfa abu Mashi, Shalouf’s mother-in-law, said in a video interview with Anadolu. “My daughter asked me, ‘Where is Iman?’ I told her she was in her tent. She went to check on her and found her covered in blood after she was hit by a bullet.”
Shalouf’s husband, Ismail abu Mashi, said “Where is the ceasefire they keep talking about? There is no such thing. There is killing every day. People are dying here every day.”
Shalouf was rushed to Nasser hospital, where doctors initially detected her unborn baby’s heartbeat, but she and her unborn baby died a few hours later.
According to relatives, Shalouf had already chosen the name Ayoub for the baby, who was due in November.
Relatives and community members gathered at the hospital to hold funeral prayers for Shalouf and her child before carrying their bodies for burial in Khan Younis. They were buried side by side.
Contacted by the Guardian, the Israel Defense Forces said they were looking into the incident.
Despite the ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025, violence and the killing of Palestinians continue on a daily basis.

The health ministry in Gaza said 10 Palestinians had been killed and 56 wounded in Israeli attacks over the previous 48 hours, amid artillery shelling and gunfire in several areas of northern, central and southern Gaza.

blocks.caption: Displaced Palestinians walk among the ruins of buildings in al-Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood east of Gaza City. Photograph: Mohammed Saber/EPA

blocks.text: Four members of the same family – Momen Ahmed, his wife, Haneen Saleh, and their daughters Lana, 12, and Bana, eight – were killed when their home in Beit Lahiya was struck on Thursday night, according to the ministry. Six other Palestinians were reported killed in Khan Younis and Gaza City on Friday, including a man who died of wounds sustained in an earlier attack.

Several other Palestinians were injured in attacks across Gaza. On Friday, two people were reportedly seriously injured in an attack in Beit Lahiya, while three people including a woman six months pregnant and a child were wounded by gunfire in the same city.
On Saturday, nine people were injured when a displaced people’s tent in al-Mawasi was shelled, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent.

On Sunday, two Palestinians were killed and several others injured when a vehicle was struck in Tel al-Hawa in Gaza City, according to the health ministry. The attack also injured people on a passing bus carrying women and children.

On 28 August, Unicef said at least four children had been reported killed in the preceding five days and many others wounded, including children who sustained life-changing injuries. On 2 September, it said three other children had reportedly been killed and at least five others injured in the preceding 24 hours, bringing the number of children reportedly killed between 23 August and 2 September to seven.

“Airstrikes by Israeli forces continue killing and wounding Palestinians,” Médecins Sans Frontières said. “Between September 6 and 9, Israeli forces issued 18 so-called evacuation orders and struck a building less than 250ft from an MSF clinic.”

The humanitarian situation remains severe. According to the UN’s humanitarian office, “most of Gaza’s 2.1 million are approaching the rainy season in overcrowded displacement sites, at risk of flooding and disease, while efforts to help them prepare are constrained by funding shortfalls and access restrictions”.
On 31 August, a temporary halt to desalination in Israel reduced the water available to about a million people in Gaza who rely on the Israeli grid.
Several electricity generators at hospitals across the Gaza Strip have stopped working because of shortages of spare parts and fuel, the territory’s health ministry has said.

According to the ministry, 1,369 Palestinians have been killed and 4,627 wounded since the fragile ceasefire took effect on 11 October 2025. Since Israel’s war in Gaza began on 7 October 2023, at least 73,783 Palestinians have been killed and 174,738 wounded, according to the ministry.

articles.title: From wards to the presidential suite: Room rates at the PGH
articles.summary: The PGH is a tertiary state-owned hospital located in Manila. Primarily funded through the UP System's budget allocation, it offers several types of rooms.

blocks.text: Published September 13, 2026 11:51pm

A few days after former House Speaker Martin Romualdez was arrested in his hospital bed at a private hospital, the Sandiganbayan ordered his transfer to the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) to verify his doctors' medical findings.

The PGH is a tertiary state-owned hospital located in Manila. It is administered and operated by the University of the Philippines Manila and is primarily funded through the UP System's budget allocation.
Romualdez was moved to the PGH on Saturday, entering through what the hospital's guards said was not the regular entryway for patients.
It has not been disclosed what room the former Speaker is in, but according to its website, PGH offers at least 10 types of rooms under its Department of Private Patient Services (DPPS).
The most affordable option is the “Ward” at a daily rate of P715, followed by “Semi-Private I” (one to three beds) at P1,000 per day, and the “Cubicle” at P1,100.
“Semi-Private II” rooms accommodate one to two beds and are priced at P1,430 daily. The final option priced below two thousand pesos is the “Studio Room” at P1,650 per day.

PGH also offers “Small Private” and “Big Private” rooms at P2,200 and P2,750, respectively, while “Superior” rooms are priced at P3,300. The PGH's 2026 Citizen’s Charter lists the price for a Big Private room at P1,500.
The two most expensive options under the DPPS are the Executive Room at P5,500 per day and the Presidential Suite, which costs P6,600 per day.

The room rates provided by PGH cover only the base daily accommodation charge and do not include additional hospital expenses such as professional fees, laboratory tests, and other medical procedures. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Obama reportedly urges Democrats to prioritize safety plan for AI
articles.summary:
Ex-president urged party at closed-door fundraiser to create sweeping framework, from safety ‘slow-down’ to job losses

Barack Obama urged Democrats to prioritize a “public conversation”…

blocks.text: Barack Obama urged Democrats to prioritize a “public conversation” about AI management and safety in a closed-door Manhattan fundraiser last week.
The comments by the former US president reportedly urged the party to create a sweeping framework for everything from a safety “slow-down” to domestic job losses and children’s wellbeing.

Obama’s comments follow a summer in which a band of rogue OpenAI chatbots hacked the company Hugging Face, towns across the country opposed datacenters and an AI researcher resigned in a viral social media post warning: “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

AI leaders have recently expressed agreement that the race for technological superiority should slow, but have also sought to appease investors, whose stake in the technology is predicted to exceed $1tn in 2026 alone.

“Once you are speaker,” Obama said to US House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, a New York-Democrat, at the fundraiser Thursday. “I would strongly urge that the Democrats put together a framework for a very public conversation,” according to a transcript first reported by the New York Times.

“This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama said. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases. I do think that this can help us figure out pathways for a clean energy future.”
Obama later added: “I would talk about this, and I would say, ‘Here’s our plan for safety. Here’s our plan for making sure our kids are not corrupted by this,’” he said according to the Times.

Obama made the remarks as the US closes in on the midterm elections and Congress has taken little action on AI. While prominent Democratic lawmakers, and some Republicans, have called to regulate the technology, Trump has attempted to aid the AI industry by introducing legislation that would ban state regulations (the bill did not move forward). Democrats face an open presidential field in 2028.

One major flashpoint for the midterm elections is datacenters that power AI companies. Both parties have since begun running ads that oppose them, as one of the few issues, “Maga Republicans and liberal Democrats” agree on, according to an NPR analysis.

On Sunday, while on a trip to his Irish golf course, Trump told reporters that a lot of “very negative forces” are ⁠bringing up concerns ⁠about ​AI that “won’t happen”, and that his main concern was that the US remain the industry leader, according to Reuters.

“We’re leading China ​in AI. ‌We’re the ‌most sophisticated country in the world, ‌and frankly I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins,” Trump told reporters when asked if ‌the AI industry should slow down or be ​more regulated.
In the past, Trump has said on social media that anyone who opposes AI datacenters is likely “backwards and poor”.

“The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor. If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign,” he said on TruthSocial two weeks ago.

articles.title: Police release images of six men sought after violent disorder in Portsmouth
articles.summary:
Hampshire and Isle of Wight force says it wants to speak to men in connection with anti-migrant unrest that left seven officers injured

Police have released images of six men they would like…

blocks.text: Police have released images of six men they would like to speak to after violent disorder in Portsmouth last week that left seven officers injured.

About 200 people gathered at Eastney Marina on Sunday night after a small boat carrying asylum seekers arrived on the south coast having crossed the Channel. The activists dispersed the following day in the early hours.
Hampshire and Isle of Wight constabulary said seven police officers were injured and treated at the scene, while vehicles belonging to the Coastguard and Border Force were damaged.
The force said it reviewed “hundreds of hours’ worth” of footage from the disorder and released images of six men it believes “can assist our investigation”.
The first person charged in connection with the demonstration in the city appeared in court on Saturday morning.
Del Leon Somerville, 42, from Paulsgrove, Portsmouth, appeared at the city’s magistrates court charged with violent disorder and assaulting a police constable.
A 16-year-old boy from Waterlooville was also arrested on suspicion of violent disorder in connection with last Sunday’s events. He has been released on bail until 12 December.
Anti-immigration activists returned to the streets of Portsmouth on Saturday afternoon, where they faced counter-protests from anti-racism groups.

Tony Rowlinson, assistant chief constable, said the scenes at Eastney Marina had gone beyond peaceful protest. “Violence and criminal damage have no part in peaceful protest,” he said. “Clearly events on Sunday evening were not peaceful protest, rather violent public disorder.”
Rowlinson said officers had worked to protect people in the area and warned that police would pursue those responsible after reviewing footage.

“The reality of public order policing is that arrests at the time are not always possible, especially where evidence may need to be reviewed to clearly identify who is responsible for offences,” he said.
He added that none of the seven injured officers had been seriously hurt, but said they “did not deserve to be assaulted” while policing the demonstration.
Police also said they were investigating online threats and abuse directed at officers and staff from partner agencies after the disorder.
The force has appealed to anyone who recognises the six men to contact police on 101 or report information online, quoting reference 44260435943.
Rowlinson said: “If you break the law we will take action against you and where it is feasible to do so seek a prosecution.”

articles.title: Trump doubles down on united Ireland comments on day two of visit
articles.summary: The US president was speaking at the Irish Open on Sunday and said "many people agree" with his comments.

blocks.text: Image source, PA Media
Donald Trump is on day two of the visit to Ireland where he will spend the day at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare, for the Irish Open
ByEnda McClafferty and Niall McCrackenin Doonbeg, County Clare
President Donald Trump has doubled down on his support for a united Ireland.
He's on day two of a visit, which he is spending at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, County Clare, for the Irish Open.
On Saturday, Trump told reporters he would love to see a united Ireland while at a meeting with the Taoiseach (Irish PM) Micheál Martin in Dublin.
Speaking on Sunday at his Doonbeg golf resort, he said it would be natural to put Ireland and Northern Ireland "together".
He spoke to reporters after watching the tournament leader Irish golfer Shane Lowry tee off.
He described what he said about a united Ireland as "a fairly routine comment".
Watch: Trump says Northern Ireland joining Ireland only natural
"I've always loved the people of Ireland. It just seems to me you have Northern Ireland and Ireland," he said
"It seems that one of the naturals of all time is to put them together.
"That's only my opinion, and by the way many people agree."
The president sidestepped a question about Scottish independence.
"I won't talk about Scotland yet I will save that," he said.
The taoiseach said the president's remarks did not come as a "surprise" to him.

Speaking on Sunday at The Open, Martin referred to Trump asking about a "merger" of Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland at an event in Washington during the Saint Patrick's Day celebrations, which some believed to be a comment on unity.
"He would make the point this is his view. He believes unity is the logical way for the island to be configured and organised," Martin said.
A major security operation is continuing for Trump's visit to Ireland.
He will leave from Shannon Airport on Sunday evening.

blocks.caption: A map showing Ireland. Doonbeg and Shannon Airport are featured.

blocks.text: Protests continue against Trump visit
More than 10,000 people marched through Dublin on Saturday to show their opposition to the US president.
Others protesting against the visit have been arriving in buses to Doonbeg on Sunday, with about 100 protesters present.
A small crowd were moved from the president's hotel by Gardai (Irish police), Irish broadcaster RTÉ is reporting.
On Saturday evening, three women were arrested for trespassing on the golf links at Doonbeg and appeared at a special sitting of Ennis District Court.
Rev Steven Foster, a Methodist minister from Galway, attended the anti-Trump protest in Doonbeg.
"I'm here because Trump is the exact opposite of everything I stand for as a follower of Jesus," he told BBC News NI.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Rev Steven Foster is in Doonbeg to protest against the visit

blocks.text: Rev Steven Foster is in Doonbeg to protest against the visit
Foster added: "As a church leader, it's important for me to be visible, and the church needs to be visible in this regard."
Foster said the "type of welcome he has been given sends out a terrible message".
Golf course is a 'massive employer'

blocks.caption: Image caption, Martin Kelly, who's a business owner, says the golf course is a "massive business" for Doonbeg

blocks.text: Martin Kelly, who's a business owner, says the golf course is a "massive business" for Doonbeg
However, others have praised Trump for the benefits and jobs his golf course brings to the local area.
Martin Kelly is a local businessman from Doonbeg and said the village is "very fortunate" to have the Trump International Golf Course.
"It's a massive employer here to be honest with you," he told BBC News NI.
"There's nothing else about here at that scale; they're very decent people to work for, they're very fair."
He said local people are "very proud" that the golf tournament is taking place there.

"We're not into politics here, we're into business. And it's a massive business to us. Doonbeg is one of the best links course in the world. Donald Trump isn't perfect but look he's not doing a bad job either.
"Hopefully Shane Lowry can win now with the help of God, and hopefully he can come to Doonbeg afterwards for a beer, I'll buy him one if he does."

blocks.caption: Image caption, Publican Seoirse Comerford says the golf course gives "a big boost" to the local economy

blocks.text: Publican Seoirse Comerford says the golf course gives "a big boost" to the local economy
Seoirse Comerford owns the Comerford bar in Doonbeg. He described the tournament as "unbelievable".
"If you look at the red double decker buses going up and down the street full of people, we never thought we would have seen the like of that."
He said the golf course is a big employer and is keeping Doonbeg "alive".
"Most rural villages in west Clare are all dying a death, young people going away to college, they don't come back.
"Like there's over 300 people employed up there at the golf course , it's a big boost to the local economy. You've got big companies in Dublin, like Intel, the golf course is our Intel down here.
"I probably wouldn't have taken over the bar business other than the golf course being up there.
"We would have had 1,000 plus through the pub on Saturday night and the same Friday night, so there's a lot of people around the village, which is great to see."
