articles.title: US congressman swims to safety after his plane is forced to land on a lake
articles.summary: The small plane carrying Rep Tom Tiffany had a mechanical issue that forced the pilot to make an emergency landing on a Wisconsin lake.

blocks.text: Wisconsin Congressman Tom Tiffany has said he sustained minor injuries after a plane he was on landed on a lake, forcing him and the pilot to swim to safety.

Tiffany, the state's Republican nominee for governor, was travelling in a small plane on Saturday night when the aircraft encountered a mechanical issue, forcing the pilot to make an emergency landing in Lake Wausau, the county sheriff's office said.
Tiffany said he and the pilot called 911 once they landed.

"As the plane began to submerge, we exited the aircraft and swam to a shallow area, where we waited until emergency responders reached us by boat," Tiffany wrote on social media. The pilot also sustained minor injuries.
Tiffany was coming home from a dinner in La Crosse County when the plane suddenly lost power as it approached Wausau Downtown Airport, he said on Sunday.

Authorities received a 911 report of a plane crash on the lake at 20:49 local time (02:49 BST), the Marathon County Sheriff's office said in a press release. The pair managed to get out of the plane and to shallow water where a Wausau Fire Department airboat rescued them about 15 minutes later, at 21:05 local time, according to the sheriff's office.
The office said Tiffany and the pilot were the only two people on board the Beechcraft K35 - a single-engine plane, also known as a Bonanza, that can carry up to five people.

"God was watching over us tonight, and I am incredibly grateful to be here in the hospital with my wife, Chris, by my side," Tiffany said. "An experience like this reminds you just how precious life is."
He received a small cut over his right eye in the incident, his campaign said.

The cause of the mechanical issue was not immediately clear, and the sheriff's office said the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board will investigate the incident.
The plane remains in the lake as emergency crews work to remove it, the office added.

articles.title: Cardinal David challenges faithful to be 'digital missionaries'
articles.summary: Caloocan Bishop Pablo Cardinal David has challenged Catholics not to simply gather "followers" or become content creators but to spread the truth, help people discern, build relationships by becoming…

blocks.text: Published September 13, 2026 11:27pm

Caloocan Bishop Pablo Cardinal David has challenged Catholics not to simply gather "followers" or become content creators but to spread the truth, help people discern, build relationships by becoming online missionaries.

"The internet can connect millions of people and still leave them terribly lonely. Algorithms can gather people into groups and still divide them into hostile camps. Your mission is not simply to gather followers. It is to build relationships, create spaces of encounter, and help people journey together," said Cardinal David in his homily at the closing Mass of the first Asian Catholic Digital Missionary Assembly held at Novaliches Cathedral.

"Every screen opens onto a human life. Every post reaches a person with hopes, fears, wounds and a dignity that no argument can erase. Before you answer a comment, share a story or enter a debate, remember: the person on the other side is not an enemy to defeat, but a brother or sister to encounter," he added.

David, speaking about the Gospel reading on forgiveness, talked about countering negative online comments and "Speak the truth with charity. Defend what is right without denying the humanity of the person who disagrees with you."
"When others spread anger, answer with courage. When others spread contempt, answer with dignity. When others close the door, become a bridge," he said.

The prelate said digital missionaries bear these traits: someone who listens, someone who accompanies, someone who makes room for others, someone who builds communion, someone who helps people discern together where the Spirit is leading us.

"And whenever the world says that hatred must have the last word, let your lives and your words proclaim the Gospel: In Christ, forgiveness is stronger than resentment, communion is stronger than division, and a new beginning is always possible," he added. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Four dead in Louisiana stabbing spree as police search for person of interest
articles.summary:
Sheriff’s office identifies Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, as person of interest after series of stabbings in Houma leaves four dead

Police are searching for a person of interest after a series of…

blocks.text: Police are searching for a person of interest after a series of stabbings in Houma, Louisiana, left at least four people dead and another person in critical condition in hospital.

The Terrebonne parish sheriff’s office identified Kaegan Jude Solet, 47, as a person of interest, after deputies were initially called to the Ashland Drive area of Houma and located a juvenile with apparent stab wounds.
The victim was airlifted to an out-of-area hospital and remains in critical condition.
As the investigation continued, authorities later found four deceased victims in a nearby home.

Solet was previously arrested in connection with a 2019 stabbing in Houma. According to a Houma police department news release, Solet, then 40, was accused of repeatedly stabbing a 59-year-old woman at a hotel following an argument.

Solet was identified as a suspect in the case when investigators learned he was a guest in the victim’s room. Officers said the pair had got into some kind of argument and Solet stabbed the victim repeatedly in the upper body and head. She was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries.
Solet was booked at the time on one count of attempted second-degree murder.

The 2019 case is separate from the current investigation. The identification of a person of interest does not constitute an arrest or criminal charge. Authorities have not announced any charges against him in the current case.
The current investigation remains ongoing as detectives continue gathering evidence and developing information surrounding the incidents.

articles.title: How could Reform UK spend its £72m of new billionaire donations?
articles.summary:
Harborne and Delo’s cash could buy a massive head start in an election, but spending big has possible pitfalls

Nigel Farage once said he could spend his £5m gift from Christopher Harborne…

blocks.text: Nigel Farage once said he could spend his £5m gift from Christopher Harborne on Ferraris if he wanted to, given its unconditional nature.

With the new donations to his party from Harborne and his fellow crypto billionaire Ben Delo of £72m over the past weekend alone, Farage’s party now has nearly enough cash to buy a Reform UK branded Ferrari for a party organiser in each of Britain’s 632 constituencies (though that would certainly be a waste and a bit of a tax headache).
But what the cash can buy first and foremost for Reform is manpower. Already the party is seeking to recruit more than 60 local organisers in key areas of the country.

Though the donation is certainly enough to staff every constituency in England, Scotland and Wales with organisers, that would also be a massive waste of resources in seats Reform UK is never likely to win. Instead, experienced regional staff can build impeccable targeting data for the seats Reform UK needs to win a majority.

Reform has already invested heavily in improving its canvassing tools and its ReformPro software – but it is boots on the ground that ensure the data being fed into those tools is as accurate as it can be. That requires door-to-door canvassing to identify switching voters and non-voters who might be persuaded to turn out.

For most parties, those kinds of local resources are only really deployed far closer to an election. Beginning that level of organising and data collection this far out could give Reform UK a massive head start at the next election, though other parties have very valuable legacy data from previous elections of which Reform has much less available.

Local parties could also print and send a many more direct mail drops, which are uncapped outside of the election period, with voters receiving “local newspapers” which are in fact Reform UK campaigning mailouts.

As well as on the ground, the cash also gives Reform UK massive potential power in the air war, on social media in particular with paid ads that can be micro-targeted locally and professionally produced and filmed. It can spend large amounts of money buying social media advertising completely legally and without limit, including on YouTube and Facebook.

Again, there will be little competition in this space as many parties will not use their resources on this so early in the electoral cycle. Already Reform has professionally built broadcast studios, and splashes the cash liberally on major policy announcements at aircraft hangars, and stadiums for rallies.

Theo Bertram, the director of the Social Market Foundation thinktank, who was previously a Labour adviser and vice-president at TikTok, said in a post on X that he believed Reform would also wish to invest the money in getting in serious policy expertise and preparation for government.

Parties often rely on goodwill from expert supporters to help prepare for government or draft their manifesto. But Reform UK could recruit some of the best legal and constitutional experts to help it find ways of implementing some of its most radical and controversial policies, including mass deportations and evicting non-UK citizens from social housing. Bertram estimates that getting the best and most expensive consultants on the issues would cost the party about £25m.

Candidate vetting has also been a nightmare for Reform and cash could be used to considerably sharpen the process. There would be a vast war chest for legal challenges – Reform UK has often threatened or begun judicial reviews of government policies – which keep the party in the headlines.

There is one way that Reform UK may come a cropper if it spends the money like water over the coming months. Should Andy Burnham call a snap general election before next autumn, election spending rules are retrospective for the previous years.

That means the spending cap, roughly £34m across Great Britain, applies for the previous 12 months, leaving the party in a bit of a trap if it has already outspent that amount outside the six-week election campaign. Might that be one reason to tempt Burnham into an early poll?

in Stockholm

items: 18m agoHej from Stockholm!

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa
in Stockholm

Evening opening: Welcome to 2026 Swedish parliamentary election live blog

articles.title: Trump reiterates $5,000 ‘dividend’ pledge if Republicans win midterms
articles.summary:
Plan to give US adults $5,000 has been greeted with incredulity across the political spectrum as well as outrage

Donald Trump on Sunday doubled down on his controversial pledge to give US…

blocks.text: Donald Trump on Sunday doubled down on his controversial pledge to give US adults a $5,000 “dividend” if his Republican ⁠party keeps control of Congress after November’s midterm elections.

The plan has been greeted with expressions of incredulity across the US political spectrum as well as outraged accusations of seeing to bribe voters. The plan – which would cost more than a trillion dollars – also comes amid huge concern over the US national debt, which topped $40tn for the first time in August.

“I don’t ‌know but ‌it’s easy if the ‌Republicans win. $5,000 to all adults in the country and we can easily handle that because we’re taking in ‌so much money,” Trump told reporters in Ireland where he is on a visit to a golf course.

Trump had been asked if ​Congress would need to approve the $5,000 pledge and continued: “The Democrats can’t make that pledge ⁠because it would all go to ​hell ​right away, ​we’d go into a ​depression … ‌I made ​that pledge, ​I always keep my pledge.”
The US has roughly 240 million adult citizens, suggesting a cost of $1.2tn. The federal government spent about $7tn in fiscal year 2025, with about $2tn taken on as debt.

When the plan was first touted by Trump last week at a rally in Texas, Marc Goldwein of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget wrote on X that “the result would be a huge spike in the deficit, and almost certainly in the inflation rate.”

Democratic political leaders also reacted with a mix of outrage, disbelief and condemnation to the remarkable suggestion which comes at a time when Trump is struggling with low poll numbers and a disastrous conflict in Iran, which is having an impact on the health of the US economy.

“After making you sicker and poorer with his war, Donald Trump now wants to buy your vote with $5,000 in taxpayer-funded blood money,” said California governor, Gavin Newsom. “The most corrupt man ever to occupy the Oval Office.”
But some Republicans have backed the idea.
“I will get a bill ready so that we can get the Trump Dividend passed immediately after the November 3rd election,” said US senator Bernie Moreno, an Ohio Republican, in a social media post on X.

items: Reuters contributed to this article

articles.title: As Japan’s yen peaks, is the era of budget-friendly trips coming to an end for Australian travellers?
articles.summary:
The currency has now reached its highest level against the US and Australian dollars in six months

  • Get our

blocks.text: In the unpredictable world of global currency markets, there has been one safe bet: that the Japanese yen would continue its relentless decline.
In recent weeks, that trade has started to unravel after Tokyo and Washington intervened to support the longsuffering Japanese currency.
The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, went so far as to dare traders to bet against bilateral efforts to bolster the yen.
While the high-stakes currency game plays out, there are emerging questions over whether the era of budget-friendly trips to Japan is coming to an end for Australian travellers.
Australians are still Tokyo dreaming

Once considered an expensive destination, a years-long decline in the value of the yen has helped a generation of Australians visit Japan, making it the third-most visited destination after Indonesia and New Zealand, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
About 1 million Australians went there in 2025-26, representing a threefold increase from a decade ago.

Numbers have surged since the pandemic reopening, at the same time as the Australian dollar has risen in value by well over 30% against the yen, bringing down the cost of shopping in Tokyo, dining in Osaka and sightseeing in Kyoto.
Dean Long, chief executive at the Australian Travel Industry Association, says it’s been a “once-in-a-generation currency position”.
“Japan has always had a high level of appeal, but suddenly people could actually do the things that they wanted to do because of the currency,” says Long.
He likens the experience to the period that ran between late 2010 and 2013 when the Australian dollar surged above parity with the US dollar.
“What your Australian dollar could do in the US was extraordinary, so people had a higher quality experience,” Long says.
‘Carry trade’ putting downward pressure on yen
Forecasting currency movements is notoriously difficult, and there’s no certainty that the yen will strengthen.
To do so, investors will need to unwind one of Wall Street’s favourite strategies which involves borrowing yen at low interest rates to invest in higher yielding currencies.
The “carry trade”, as it is known, has historically put downward pressure on the yen.

Japanese authorities want to halt a plummeting currency that has driven up energy and food import costs, while the US recently joined the effort to deter Tokyo from selling US treasuries, which drives up the US government’s own borrowing costs.
after newsletter promotion
The Japanese currency has now reached its highest level against the US and Australian dollars in about six months, raising the possibility that a longer-term trend is setting in.
Analysts at IG have noted that if the yen breaks through a series of technical levels, then “all bets are off” and it could rise to levels not seen since 2023.
Japan must compete with Vietnam and ‘Chinamaxxing’
Joseph Cheer, professor of sustainable tourism and heritage at Western Sydney University, says he wouldn’t expect a change in travel habits even if Japan became moderately more expensive to visit.
“There’s a great deal of tolerance before Australians would start rethinking about whether Japan is a good value proposition,” says Cheer.
He says a sustained rise in the yen could, however, open the door for other Asian nations offering competitively priced holidays to entice Australian tourists away from Japan.
Vietnam is recording huge interest from Australians, with annual visits now more than double what they were a decade ago.

There is also a “Chinamaxxing” social media trend of younger people interested in Chinese culture. More Australians visited China last financial year than the US, in a reversal of long-term holiday trends.
“There’s been a cultural turn in the last decade where Australians are looking more towards Asia, rather than travelling long-haul,” says Cheer.
“South Korea can give Japan a real run for its money and everyone’s trying to fill up on Chinese culture, which is going to be very stiff competition especially if Japan becomes more expensive.”

articles.title: Crossbench MPs launch push to stop Australian military exports being used in human rights breaches
articles.summary:
‘Red lines’ legislation would forbid defence equipment technology or services being used, includes parts for F-35 fighter jets

  • Get our

blocks.text: Crossbench MPs including David Pocock and Sophie Scamps will put pressure on the Albanese government to ban Australian goods from being used by the Israeli military – including for F-35 fighter jets – by introducing a bill designed to force it to adhere to international obligations.

The group’s “red lines” legislation, to be presented on Monday, would outlaw defence equipment, technology or services being used where they could breach Australia’s international human rights obligations.

They hope the bill would end Australia’s involvement in manufacturing parts of the F-35 aircraft used by the Israeli air force in Gaza to “strike terror targets and assist ground forces in very close proximity strikes” – which the government has been under increasing pressure to stop.
“Of all the issues many people contact me about, human rights and the Gaza genocide is by far the biggest,” Pocock said.
“I have received thousands of emails from Canberrans desperately concerned by the indiscriminate killing we have seen overseas.”

The foreign minister, Penny Wong, has previously described Australia’s contributions to the F-35 supply chain as “non-lethal in nature”. The defence minister, Richard Marles, has accused critics of “misinformation” and said Australia has contributed to program for decades as part of a multi-lateral agreement with Lockheed Martin in the US, rather than with Israel directly.

The prime minister was roundly criticised last week, including from within his own ranks, for not following the UK and other like-minded countries in banning trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

The crossbench group – which also includes the Greens and independents Lidia Thorpe, Andrew Wilkie and Fatima Payman – say their bill could also prevent companies and institutions investing in activities connected to illegal settlements and serious international law violations.
The proponents of the laws say they would put Australia’s legislation in line with its international human rights obligations, and establish an independent anti-genocide commissioner.
Large companies, defence businesses and commonwealth entities would also be forced to report and intervene on genocide risks in their operations and supply chains.
The Greens’ deputy leader, Mehreen Faruqi, challenged the government to “prove that all their talk about international law and human rights actually means something”.

“This package is far from radical and delivers exactly what Australians expect of their government. Australian governments and corporations should not be sending military parts, trading with, or profiting from, a genocide,” she said.
after newsletter promotion

The bills are backed by international law advocates and experts including the former president of the Australian Human Rights Commission, Gillian Triggs, and the executive director of the Australian Centre for International Justice, Rawan Arraf.
Scamps said the legislation would help ensure business and the government were not “unknowingly complicit in war crimes and genocide and other human rights violations”.
“This is not about a single country, there are grievous human rights abuses going on all around the world,” she said.
“It is not nearly good enough for our government to say they are not sure if components we manufacture here in Australia are being used in F-35s that have killed tens of thousands of people in Gaza.”

Thorpe said bill – to be concurrently introduced in the house and Senate this week – was about upholding fundamental human rights that the government “is already committed to under international law”.
Labor is not expected to support the private member’s bill.

articles.title: Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce stayed at Gina Rinehart’s $20m mansion after One Nation fundraisers
articles.summary:
Exclusive: New details underscoring depth of relationship between billionaire and party revealed in first episode of Guardian podcast The Populist

  • Listen to the…

blocks.text: Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce stayed overnight at Gina Rinehart’s $20m Brisbane mansion after fundraising events held for One Nation, Guardian Australia can reveal.
On one occasion, Joyce conducted a live television interview with Channel Seven’s Sunrise program from a room that appears to be a bedroom in Rinehart’s home.
The interview took place on Monday 13 April, the morning after a fundraising event at the mining magnate’s house on the banks of the Brisbane River in Hawthorne.

The new details underscoring the depth of the relationship between Australia’s richest person and One Nation have been revealed in the first episode of the Guardian’s new podcast about the party, The Populist, released on Monday.

Parliamentary expenditure records show that Hanson and Joyce declared flights on 13 April courtesy of Hancock Prospecting, with flight-tracking data showing that the pair flew on Rinehart’s luxury Gulfstream jet from Brisbane to Sydney that afternoon.

blocks.caption: Barnaby Joyce speaks to Channel Seven’s Sunrise program from Gina Rinehart’s house

blocks.text: The accommodation at Rinehart’s home has not been declared to the parliament, which has rules in place mandating that gifts or hospitality valued at more than $300 – or any interest “where a conflict of interest with a [parliamentarian]’s public duties could foreseeably arise or be seen to arise” – should be declared.

The guidelines state that “hospitality” refers to “free or concessional accommodation” provided to the MP, the MP’s spouse or partner or dependent children “wholly or partly by any person, organisation, business or interest group or foreign government or its representative”.

The provision of meals or accommodation excludes “hospitality provided in a purely social way by friends or colleagues”, but the guidelines are designed to place on the public record interests that may conflict, or be seen to conflict, with an MP’s public duty.
Joyce told Guardian Australia that Rinehart “was a long-term friend over decades not a motel”.
“When I stay with family or friends they don’t charge me, nor do I see it as work,” he said.
“I will never be ashamed of doing the research to do a better job.”
Guardian Australia can also reveal that Hanson has been using one of Rinehart’s bodyguards for her personal security.
The man, who has been seen escorting Hanson in Perth and Canberra, has been one of Rinehart’s closest bodyguards for more than a decade.

The New South Wales supreme court heard in 2013 that Rinehart had asked the bodyguard to offer one of her daughters, Bianca Rinehart, a $25m loan to pull out of a court battle contesting the family trust. The offer was rejected.
after newsletter promotion

According to his LinkedIn, the man works as a security manager with an undeclared company but a post from 2023 shows him listed as an employee of Hancock Energy. It is unclear if he remains employed by Hancock Prospecting.
Guardian Australia has previously reported multiple breaches of Senate rules, with One Nation failing to declare flights gifted by Hancock Prospecting to Hanson going back to August last year.

The fresh details of the company’s financial support for One Nation come despite Hanson telling reporters in February she was not being funded by Rinehart, and after the party’s national director, James Ashby, said in December last year: “We have not seen any money from her.”
The Labor senator Murray Watt criticised Hanson for failing to disclose the links between her party and Rinehart, including the undeclared flights.

“I think that the lengths that she and her colleagues have gone repeatedly to conceal donations, staffing matters, all sorts of other things about their operations, it does make you think that there’s something to hide,” Watt told the Guardian.

“In a democratic system like Australia, there is a responsibility of politicians to be transparent about decision making, about their operations, and again Pauline Hanson seems to want to get all the benefits of power without any of the responsibilities of power.
“The level of concealment that goes on suggests a guilty conscience.

“I think that one of the reasons that One Nation goes to such efforts to conceal their financial gain from Gina Rinehart and her companies is because there is such a close alignment between what Gina Rinehart and Hancock want to see happen and One Nation’s policies.”
One Nation did not respond to questions from Guardian Australia.
A spokesperson for Hancock Prospecting said: “Donations will be disclosed in accordance with applicable laws and reporting requirements.”

articles.title: Turkish authorities launch crackdown on 2SLGBTQ+ and HIV support groups
articles.summary: Turkish authorities cracked down on multiple 2SLGBTQ+ groups and individuals early Sunday morning, detaining dozens of members, breaking into association offices and raiding popular hangouts.

image.caption: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is shown at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, on Sept. 1. (Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Pool Sputnik/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
Turkish authorities cracked down on multiple 2SLGBTQ+ groups and individuals early Sunday morning, detaining dozens of members, breaking into association offices and raiding popular hangouts.
Raids mark escalation of decade-long hostility toward groups ahead of election

In an escalation of its decade-long hostility toward 2SLGBTQ+ groups, particularly in the lead-up to elections, simultaneous police raids beginning at 1 a.m. took place in the major cities of Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydin and Mersin.

Justice Minister Akin Gürlek announced on social media that the investigation into 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses was to "protect children, the institution of the family, and public order" in line with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s 10-year executive order relating to families and children.

"As per the duty to protect families and children given to the state by the constitution, no criminal organization, abuse network or illegal activity which targets children, youths or families will be tolerated!" Gürlek said.
The raids targeted both current and former members of multiple prominent 2SLGBTQ+ rights and HIV awareness groups. The organizations’ websites were also blocked.
Gürlek also said that such associations were found to receive significant funding from international sources and agencies.

The Human Rights Association condemned the raids. "This is not a judicial investigation; it is a political operation aimed at forcing society into a monolithic family model and purging LGBTI+ and independent civil society under the guise of protecting the family and children," it said.

items: Egypt blocks entry to 2SLGBTQ+ cruise days after Turkey did the same

blocks.text: "To include unrelated charges such as 'forming a criminal organization,' 'drugs,' 'prostitution' and 'obscenity' serves not to reveal the truth but to incriminate the entire community."
The religious conservative Justice and Development Party, led by Erdogan, has been increasingly vocal against 2SLGBTQ+ groups to play up to the more conservative elements of its base.
In 2015, the party banned Istanbul Pride, which had tens of thousands of attendees in previous years prior. Since then, authorities have violently dispersed any attempted gatherings to mark Pride.
This summer, a 2SLGBTQ+ cruise ship that tours the Mediterranean and has docked in Turkey multiple times in the past was refused permission to dock there.
The Ottoman Empire, predecessor to the modern republic of Turkey, decriminalized homosexuality in 1858, but there is still significant social discrimination.

articles.title: Russian drone hits Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train near Polish border
articles.summary:
No casualties reported as Ukraine’s foreign minister says ‘Putin’s terror knocking directly on doors of EU and Nato’

A passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw was hit by a Russian…

blocks.text: A passenger train travelling from Kyiv to Warsaw was hit by a Russian drone two kilometres from the Polish border, in an attack that Ukraine’s foreign minister described as “Putin’s terror knocking directly on the doors of the EU and Nato”.

At least six people were killed and more than 40 injured in overnight attacks across Ukraine, which involved more than 450 drones and missiles launched by Russia. Ukraine’s air force said that it intercepted 405 drones and four missiles.
Western Ukraine, which is typically quieter than Kyiv or the eastern frontline zones, was particularly badly hit.
The strikes prompted air raid warnings in Poland, which shares a border with western Ukraine.
Ukrainian and Polish authorities said a truck less than one kilometre from the Dorohusk-Yahodyn border crossing between the two countries was also hit.
Reuters reported that Russia’s defence ministry said it had targeted infrastructure that facilitated military cargoes from Europe into Ukraine.
Katerina Sergatskova, director of Daily Humanity, an organisation that provides training to people working in high-risk environments, was travelling on the Warsaw-bound train.

She said passengers were told to evacuate at around 9am as the train approached the Polish border, having already been off-boarded for two hours in the middle of the night. “At this point, the mood was different, we were asked to move very fast,” she said. “Then I heard the first drone.”
Sergatskova added: “Seeing and hearing Shahed [drones] just a few hundred meters from the border is a very unpleasant experience.”
No casualties were reported on the train. Three people were killed in the eastern Donetsk region, while one person, a 71-year-old woman, was killed in the southern Mykolaiv region.
Andrii Sybiha, Ukraine’s foreign minister, said the Russian strikes were “not just a continuation of its attacks on our state borders”.
“This is Putin’s terror knocking directly on the doors of the EU and Nato. Russian barbarians are at your gate, dear partners,” he wrote on X.

Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, wrote on Telegram: “Ukrainians are fighting every day to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe, giving their lives and preventing the aggression from expanding.”
after newsletter promotion
Poland’s foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, who visited Kyiv this week, said on X after Sunday morning’s attack: “Putin is escalating.”
The Polish interior minister, Marcin Kierwiński, said: “We treat these events with the utmost seriousness. The situation is being monitored continuously. Russia is the enemy of the free world.”
Ukraine and Russia have increased attacks on critical infrastructure in each other’s countries as long-range drones and missiles take the war further away from the frontlines.
The US president, Donald Trump, said on Sunday that Zelenskyy should “stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia” because it was causing shortages.

“Let him go after targets, but not diesel fuel, because he’s causing a shortage of diesel,” Trump said, adding that shortages were caused by the Russia-Ukraine war rather than the US war in the Middle East.

In Lithuania, authorities briefly closed the airport in Vilnius, the capital, after a perceived drone sighting. Nato summoned at least one fighter jet in response to the alert, which turned out to be a flock of birds. The airport re-opened within 40 minutes, according to Lithuanian authorities.

articles.title: Marcos on VP Sara: 'You cannot force anyone to love you'
articles.summary: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. reacts to the statements issued by Vice President Sara Duterte, who is facing an impeachment trial and a grave threats charge at a Quezon City trial court.

blocks.text: Published September 13, 2026 10:34pm
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. reacts to the statements issued by Vice President Sara Duterte, who is facing an impeachment trial and a grave threats charge at a Quezon City trial court.

"You know I hear about them, I don't really have a response. She's very angry. I suppose with what's happening to her. And I am the target of that anger... or the main target for that anger," Marcos told reporters.
"What can I do?...You cannot force anyone to love you," he added.

The Vice President on Friday on Friday called on President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. to step down from office during a rally at the Quezon City Hall following her supposed arraignment in relation to her grave threats charges. The arraignment was postponed due to the motion filed by Duterte's camp.
"Patuloy tayong manawagan ng paglayas ng problema ng ating bayan na ang pangalan ay Bongbong Marcos. Resign! Umalis ka dyan!" Duterte told her supporters.
(Let us continue to clamor that our nation's problem would leave. The name of that problem is Bongbong Marcos. Resign! Leave!)
Members of the media asked for his reaction to the statements issued by the Vice President during a press conference at the sidelines of the BRIC Summit in India.
The BRICS Summit is an annual meet between heads of state as a means of consultation and cooperation on different global issues.

Marcos had been invited by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and is set to have a bilateral meeting with him. The President said that he will also meet with Indian companies and other key players. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Turkish police detain dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists
articles.summary: Human rights groups in Turkey have accused the government of using a family- values campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community.

blocks.text: Police in Turkey have detained 47 people in a series of raids on gay bars and the homes of LGBTQ+ activists, officials say.
Raids took place in 12 provinces over the weekend as part of a campaign dubbed "My Family is Safe" that the Turkish government says has been designed to protect family values.
One of the targets of the operation was LGBTQ+ association Kaos GL.
Same-sex marriage is not recognised in Turkey, with growing pressure on gay couples. Human rights groups in Turkey have accused the government of using the campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community.
Officers detained 26 people and seized drugs, digital equipment, smuggled alcohol and a firearm during the raids, according to the Istanbul chief prosecutor's office.
In a separate statement, the Ankara chief prosecutor's office said another 21 people had been detained as part of an investigation into Kaos GL.
The organisation said 50 activists had been detained, more than 10 taken after police raids on their homes.
It said that authorities had blocked several websites and social media accounts linked to LGBTQ+ organisations.

According to the group, authorities have accused Kaos GL of making "obscenity" in online posts that are available to children and had demanded the shutting down of the Kaos GL X account, as well as those of around 15 other LGBTQ+ organisations.
Same-sex relations are not an offence in Turkey but homophobia is common, with President Recep Tayyip Erdogan describing LGBTQ people as "perverts" responsible for the falling birth rate.

As part of "My Family is Safe", Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek says legal proceedings have been started against more than 160 people and a number of organisations and companies across the country.
Gurlek did not say how many people had been taken into custody, but said the raids came in the context of the "Decade of the Family" campaign.
However, the Turkish Human Rights Association says the Turkish government has been using the campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community in recent years.
"The real name of this operation is not 'My Family is Safe'; it is state-led discrimination, politics of fear and the dismantling of civil society," the organisation said on X.

articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Sunday said that he is "happy" about the Supreme Court's decision to overturn his mother Imelda Marcos's graft conviction.

blocks.text: Published September 13, 2026 10:04pm
NEW DELHI — President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Sunday said that he is "happy" about the Supreme Court's decision to overturn his mother Imelda Marcos's graft conviction.

In its ruling—dated June 10, 2026, but made public on September 9—the Supreme Court overturned the former first lady's conviction over her alleged financial interests in seven Swiss foundations, saying the prosecution failed to prove her guilt beyond reasonable doubt.

"It's been hanging over our heads for 40 years. All those cases were filed in 1986 and that's how long it's taken. Of course, I'm happy that she does not have to be worries. because she does worry. I'm glad, especially for my mom," the President said at a press conference on the sidelines of the BRICS summit.

In 2018, the Sandiganbayan found Imelda, then 89, guilty of seven counts of graft, saying that the Swiss foundations—Maler Establishment, Trinidad Foundation, Rayby Foundation, Palmy Foundation, Vibur Foundation, Aguamina Foundation, and Avertina Foundation—were specifically created to serve as benefactors for its lone recipient, the Marcos family.
It sentenced Imelda to six to 11 years in prison for each count. However, she did not serve any prison time.
When asked about the concerns over the possible influence of this decision in the choice of the next Chief Justice, Marcos said it is not even something that crossed his mind.
"That's the first time I made any connection between the choice of Chief Justice. That will never enter our thinking in any way," he said. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Legendary Canadian boxer George Chuvalo dies aged 89
articles.summary: The heavyweight champion took on the likes of Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, and was known for never once getting knocked out or knocked down.

blocks.text: "George Chuvalo was a heavyweight boxing legend, a family friend and a Canadian icon," Ontario Premier Doug Ford wrote on social media.
"My thoughts are with all of George's family and loved ones as we mourn his passing."
After retiring from professional boxing in 1978, Chuvalo travelled the country as a public speaker advocating for anti-drug education and mental health awareness.
Chuvalo lost three sons and his wife to drug overdoses and suicide, he has said.

"I'd like to think if you're ever tempted with the idea of doing drugs, or you ever flirt with doing drugs, I hope you think of me, George Chuvalo, and what drugs did to my family," he once said, according to a CBC Radio report in 1998.
In retirement, Chuvalo also dipped his toes in acting, appearing in the 1998 comedy film Dirty Work and alongside Jeff Goldblum in the 1986 horror film The Fly.
He also served as a guest commentator for major boxing matches and co-hosted a TV boxing program called Greatest Knockouts with his friend and fellow fighter Charles "Spider" Jones.
Chuvalo is survived by his eldest son Mitch, daughter Vanessa, grandchildren, and second wife Joanne.
He died on Saturday, his birthday, said Sully's Boxing Gym.

articles.title: Kamala Harris’s California home targeted by trespasser, officials say
articles.summary:
Former vice-president and her husband were not home when person entered their property, no arrests were made

Law enforcement officials and a spokesperson for former vice-president Kamala…

blocks.text: Law enforcement officials and a spokesperson for former vice-president Kamala Harris said a trespasser was stopped at her Malibu home in California on Friday night.
Neither the former vice-president nor her husband, Doug Emhoff, were home at the time.

“Security personnel stopped an individual who illegally entered Vice-President Harris and Second Gentleman Emhoff’s property before the individual reached the home,” Harris spokesperson Eduardo Negrón said in a statement on Saturday, reported by Politico. “Vice-President Harris and Second Gentleman Emhoff were not present. They are grateful to the security and law enforcement personnel who responded swiftly.”

Los Angeles county sheriff’s deputies were sent to Harris’s home around 10.30pm that Friday night, after private security had stopped the individual. The individual was asked to leave, and no arrests were made.
The incident was originally reported by TMZ.

Vice-presidents in the US typically receive six months of Secret Service protection after leaving office. Former president Joe Biden extended Harris’s security detail to 18 months before leaving office. That extension was canceled in August 2025 by Donald Trump. Ex-presidents typically receive security protection for life.

Harris bought the home in the Point Dume area of Malibu for $8.1m this May, which prompted speculation that she would not run for president again. The celebrity studded retreat is typically seen as a place where people “downshift”, according to a Politico article at the time.

articles.summary: COTABATO CITY — Two separate explosions were reported in this city on Sunday night, a day before the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections, with one person injured in the first incident and no…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY — Two separate explosions were reported in this city on Sunday night, a day before the Bangsamoro parliamentary elections, with one person injured in the first incident and no casualties reported in the second, police said.

Police Regional Office Bangsamoro Autonomous Region (PROBAR) said the first explosion occurred at about 8 p.m. in Purok Amirol of Barangay Kalanganan, where Zainodin Sapal Macabuat, a resident of Poblacion 1, was waiting for his construction foreman.
Police said Macabuat reported seeing a flash of white light before hearing an explosion that caused him to drop to the ground. He later discovered that he had sustained injuries.
Police personnel led by Maj. Eduardo Malicdem, station commander, responded to the area at about 8:10 p.m. after receiving a report from a concerned citizen.
Police said the identity of the person behind the incident and the motive remained undetermined. The Cotabato City Explosive Ordnance Disposal team was conducting clearing operations at the scene.
Another explosion was reported at about 8:10 p.m. in Datu Udtog Matalam, Malagapas in Barangay Rosary Heights 10.
Police Station 2 said its personnel and duty investigators, led by Maj. Tugaya Alfonso, station commander, proceeded to the area after receiving a report from a concerned citizen.

Responding officers confirmed that an explosion had occurred and initially found scattered pieces of rubbish at the scene. The explosion was initially believed to have originated from a pile of garbage, police said.
No casualties were reported in the second incident.
Police requested the Cotabato City Explosive Ordnance Disposal and Chemical Unit to process the scene.
Authorities have yet to establish whether the two explosions were related or whether explosive devices were involved. /mcm

articles.title: Turkey: 162 arrested in LGBTQ+ raids
articles.summary: Turkish authorities have arrested at least 162 people in a weekend crackdown on the country's LGBTQ+ community. Ankara says police raids on gay bars and other venues are aimed at protecting family…

image.caption: Although same-sex relationships are not illegal in Turkey, the LGBTQ+ community faces harsh repression under the country's authoritarian leader, President Recep Tayyip ErdoganImage: Murat Kocabas/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: Turkish police have arrested at least 162 people and searched the offices of six LGBTQ+ associations in weekend raids designed to support the country's campaign to protect family values.

The Ankara-based LGBTQ+ rights group Kaos GL claimed that beyond arrests, the government had also cut access to dozens of websites and social media accounts belonging to associate groups and rights advocates.
Government says its fulfilling duty to 'protect families and children'

Turkish Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said investigations — prompted by accusations of prostitution and obscenity — were coordinated by prosecutors in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir, Aydin and Mersin and involved judicial proceedings against 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses across 15 provinces.

"As per the duty to protect families and children given to the state by the constitution, no criminal organization, abuse network or illegal activity which targets children, youths or families will be tolerated!" Gurlek added in a social media post.

Authorities say they seized drugs, digital equipment, smuggled alcohol and a gun in weekend police operations targeting gay bars and night clubs as well as a hammam that was said to be a place of prostitution.
The Istanbul prosecutor's office added that it had found evidence indicating that children and minors were being inappropriately swayed on issues tied to sexual orientation and gender identity.
Rights groups say the government is unfairly targeting the LGBTQ+ community, with Kaos GL saying that it had been accused of making "posts containing obscenities" accessible to children.
Being gay in Turkey
Erdogan scapegoats LGBTQ+ 'perverts' for falling birthrates, avoiding actual contributing factors

The weekend police operation was dubbed "My Family is Safe" by the government and was part of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's "Decade of Family and Population" scheme, which is designed to reverse plummeting birthrates in the aging country.

Authorities say it was intended to make sure that society does not see LGBTQ+ activity as "normal" and that raids were carried out to "protect children, the institution of the family, and our shared moral values."
Although same-sex relations are not illegal in the country, homophobia is rife, with President Erdogan blaming LGBTQ "perverts" for Turkey's rapidly declining birthrates.

That would seem a rhetorical diversion from the actual complexity of reasons for the decline, which Erdogan — who has ruled as the country's authoritarian president since 2014 as well as serving as its influential prime minister for 10 years before that — has called "a disaster."

Though Turkey's statistical agency, TurkStat, tracked a sharp decline in the total fertility rate between 2013 and 2023 (from 2.11 to 1.51 ), the shift brings birthrates in the country closer to those in other developed nations.
Observers say the real reasons for the drop are more likely of a structural and institutional nature rather than one chalked up to lifestyle.

Turkey's chronically worsening financial crisis, inflation, skyrocketing housing prices, family unfriendly workplace environments, limited access to affordable childcare, and higher educational and employment rates for women are all considered reasons for Turks to postpone having children, as well as for having fewer when they finally do.

articles.title: Prosecution spox flags confi fund receipts issued across 300 areas in one day
articles.summary: Acknowledgment receipts (ARs) covering around 300 confidential fund transactions of Vice President Sara Duterte show that the funds were distributed in a single day, House prosecution spokesperson…

blocks.text: SARA DUTERTE IMPEACHMENT TRIAL
Published September 13, 2026 9:02pm

Acknowledgment receipts (ARs) covering around 300 confidential fund transactions of Vice President Sara Duterte show that the funds were distributed in a single day, House prosecution spokesperson and Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said Sunday.
In a statement, Adiong said this raised logistical questions, on top of concerns over the identities of the fund recipients.
“Dito ho, nakita na hindi lang po yung mga ARs ang walang mga matches doon sa kanilang entries sa PSA (Philippine Statistics Authority)—questionable 'yung mga edad,” Adiong said.
(Here, we saw that it’s not just the AR entries that don’t match the PSA—the ages listed are questionable.)

“Questionable ‘yung mga panahong nakatanggap sila dahil may acknowledgment receipts na tumanggap ng dalawang beses sa isang araw at nagkaroon lang po ng disbursement sa ilang lugar, mahigit-kumulang 300 areas all over the country na distributed in one day,” he added.

(And the timing of when they received the funds is also questionable because there are acknowledgment receipts showing individuals receiving payments twice in a single day, while disbursements occurred across roughly 300 areas nationwide, all in one day.)
Adiong said these spatial and temporal inconsistencies added another layer to the prosecution’s questions over the ARs.
This echoes earlier questions raised by senator-judges about how confidential fund disbursements could have been made in distant locations on the same dates.

Adiong also said the mere existence of ARs and liquidation reports could not establish that the recorded transactions actually took place, stressing the need to prove that they represented actual transactions and legitimate expenses.

“Hindi po sapat ang acknowledgment receipts lamang o certification o liquidation reports dahil kailangan mapatunayan na ang mga ito ay tumutukoy sa totoong transaksyon at totoong paggastos,” Adiong said.
(Acknowledgment receipts, certifications or liquidation reports alone are not enough because it must be proven that these refer to actual transactions and genuine expenditures.)

Article 1 of the impeachment complaint accuses Duterte of committing impeachable offenses through the systematic misappropriation and irregular liquidation of confidential funds, involving P500 million released to the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and P112.5 million to the Department of Education (DepEd).

During earlier impeachment trial proceedings, the PSA said several recipient names submitted by the OVP and DepEd had no matching birth, marriage or death records. Other single-name matches corresponded to deceased individuals or minors. — MCG, GMA News

articles.title: World's tallest totem pole comes down in Alert Bay, B.C., after more than 50 years
articles.summary: The world’s tallest totem pole was brought down this week in Alert Bay, B.C., a community off the coast of northeast Vancouver Island. For two 'Na̱mǥis chiefs, the pole — recognized in the Guinness…

image.caption: Due to structural safety concerns, the totem pole in Alert Bay, B.C., was brought down on Sept. 9, 2026. (Submitted by Hazel Cook)

blocks.text: British Columbia

The world’s tallest totem pole was brought down this week in Alert Bay, B.C., a community off the coast of northeast Vancouver Island. For two 'Na̱mǥis chiefs, the pole — recognized in the Guinness Book of World Records — represented much more than its height.
Emotional day as the tallest totem pole in the world, representing unity between tribes, comes down
The world’s tallest totem pole was brought down this week in Alert Bay, B.C., a community off the coast of northeast Vancouver Island.
For two 'Na̱mǥis chiefs, the pole — recognized in the Guinness Book of World Records — represented much more than its height.
"This pole was so much more," said Ho’miskanis Don Svanvik, hereditary chief and elected chief councillor of the 'Na̱mǥis First Nation.
"It was a beacon for our people coming out of a pretty dark time in history," he said, referencing the potlatch ban — the federal law that outlawed potlatching on the coast for more than 60 years.
Svanvik said his great-grandparents were jailed in the 1920s for taking part in potlatch.
"The pole, in some ways, represents people being who they always have been and continue to be," he said.

items: Mi'kmaw mask carver wins Canadian Crafts Federation award
Members of Okanagan Indian Band mourn loss of forests and irreplaceable artifacts in wildfire

blocks.text: "This is who we are. This is how we govern ourselves. This is how we celebrate and acknowledge things, through our ceremonies … this was a time when that was all coming back, coming into the forefront of things."

Crews began dismantling the 173-foot pole on Wednesday in a carefully staged, multi-hour process, after the 'Na̱mǥis First Nation confirmed the structure had become too unstable and hazardous to remain standing.
The nearby Gukwdzi (Big House) and its surrounding parking area were closed the evening before to establish a safety perimeter, and community members gathered nearby to witness.
Nothing lasts forever
The original pole was raised in 1973. It was one tree spliced into two connected sections, according to 'Na̱mǥis Hereditary Chief William Wasden Jr.
He said the pole was designed to carry the crests of 22 Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw tribes — a deliberate statement of unity.
Tribes have amalgamated since then, Wasden said, but it was a powerful symbol of solidarity, an essential theme of the times.
"Our Big House was finished around then too … it was the same theme … somewhere for everybody to come and utilize," Wasden Jr. said.

"Alert Bay was like Grand Central Station, it was almost like the center of Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw territories physically, but people were amalgamating there and so it almost became Kwakwa̱ka̱ʼwakw central."
When the pole came down, Wasden said he felt proud.
"Nothing lasts forever, especially the cedar tree," he said, sharing a story of an ancestor who recognized in ancient times that neither a cedar tree nor a mountain would always stand.
For Wasden, the pole’s takedown is part of a much older pattern, one where each generation is left to answer for itself.
"It’s our ancestors challenging us now," he said. "Are you gonna ride on our coattails, or will you be as great as we were, by doing the things you need to do to uplift your people?"
The pole was carved by a number of carvers at the time, overseen by Jimmy Dick.
Wasden named Jimmy Dick’s son "Blackie," Ben Dick Senior, as the main carver. He named other carvers like Adam Dick, Andy "Beanie" Beans, Gus Matilpi and Dick Dawson.
Svanvik named Henry Hunt and Henry Speck, along with others who may have dropped in at the time.
LISTEN | The day the totem pole was taken down:
All Points West9:10World's tallest totem pole comes down
Both acknowledged Dora Cook who learned to carve alongside the men, one of very few women to do so at the time.
"She was ahead of her time," said Wasden.
Both Wasden and Svanvik remember the pole being carved when they were kids.

Svanvik jokingly said he played a small role when he was called over by the carvers to "squirt oil on the saw" they were using. Wasden carries a photo of himself and his friends sitting on the pole before it was raised.
Both said they look forward to what’s next.
"This is not the end of anything," Svanvik said.

articles.summary: Ukrainian officials accused Russia of a "systemic attack" on its railways following drone strikes near the Polish border, including a hit on a locomotive of a passenger train headed to Warsaw.

image.caption: No casualties were reported following the drone strikes near PolandImage: Sylwester Uchanski/REUTERS

blocks.text: Russia launched two drone strikes on western Ukraine, very near its border with NATO member Poland, Ukrainian and Polish authorities said on Sunday.
One of the drones hit a passenger train locomotive in Volyn, some two kilometers (1.24 miles) from the border crossing.
"The monitoring team gave the train crew advanced warning, and thanks to that, no one was injured," Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said in online post.
Putin rejects Zelenskyy's G20 talks offer
The company later said that a "systemic attack" was happening throughout Ukraine.
Separately, Poland's PKP Intercity confirmed that they have taken control of the affected train following the attack in the Ukrainian territory.
"The train is carrying 206 people. There are no Polish citizens among the passengers," the operator said online. "After completing customs clearance, it will continue its journey towards Warsaw."
Zelenskyy: Locomotive 'deliberately burned'
On Sunday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the locomotive was "deliberately burned" and a gas station damaged in Volyn.
"It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand," he said.
Moscow did not immediately comment on the reports.

blocks.caption: Falling debris set a gas station on fire near the border checkpoint in VolynImage: Sylwester Uchanski/REUTERS

blocks.text: Ukrainian officials also reported another drone strike on Yahodyn overnight, some half a mile (800 meters) from the Polish border.
The border with Poland serves as essential transit point for military and humanitarian aid.
'Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors' — Ukrainian foreign minister
Commenting on the Yahodyn incident, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the "barbaric" attacks were more than "just a continuation of its attacks on our state borders."
"This is Putin's terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and NATO. Russian barbarians are at your gate, dear partners," he said in an English-language post on X.

He urged Ukraine's Western allies to make Russia "feel the consequences of its terror. Not just half-decisions, but uncompromising, powerful steps. Full trade embargo. Full entry bans. Full sanctions on the military-industrial complex."
"Putin needs to understand that his barbarism will be met with decisive action that increases the cost of war for him to an unacceptable level," he added.

articles.title: Search underway for about 130 people after Indonesian ferry overturns
articles.summary: A ferry overturned in bad weather in Indonesia’s Java Sea on Sunday, leaving about 130 passengers and crew missing, rescuers said. At least 107 people were rescued and the bodies of six passengers…

image.caption: People look for the names of their family members on a passenger list after a ferry overturned in bad weather in the Java Sea, at the rescuers command centre in Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan, Indonesia, on Sunday. (Iman Satria/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

A ferry overturned in bad weather in Indonesia’s Java Sea on Sunday, leaving about 130 passengers and crew missing, rescuers said. At least 107 people were rescued and the bodies of six passengers were recovered.
Captain reported rough seas with waves up to 3 metres before issuing distress call

A ferry overturned in bad weather in Indonesia’s Java Sea on Sunday, leaving about 130 passengers and crew missing, rescuers said. At least 107 people were rescued and the bodies of six passengers were recovered as the search operation expanded around the vessel’s last known position.
The ferry with more than 240 people was travelling from Surabaya in East Java to Banjarmasin in South Kalimantan province, on Borneo Island, officials said.

The vessel’s captain had reported rough seas with waves up to three metres before issuing a distress call, saying the ship was listing, said I Putu Sudayana, who heads the Banjarmasin Search and Rescue Office. Authorities later received information indicating the vessel had overturned.
The rescue agency in Banjarmasin said it received a report two hours after contact was lost with the Virgo Transport 8 at about 2 a.m. on Sunday.

A rescue ship was headed to the vessel’s last known position, Sudayana said, and by Sunday afternoon authorities were deploying teams supported by eight vessels, including four navy ships, and two helicopters.
Survivors rescued, dead bodies recovered

Initial information indicated the vessel’s last known position was in the Java Sea, about 148 kilometres from Banjarmasin. The ship’s manifest said it was carrying 243 people — 213 passengers and 30 crew members — although it is common in Indonesia for the number of passengers to differ from the manifest. The vessel was also transporting 89 vehicles.
Sudayana, who is co-ordinating the search, said teams, assisted by nearby tugboats and other passing vessels, had rescued 107 people and recovered six bodies by Sunday afternoon.
The 119-metre Virgo Transport 8 ferry was built in Japan in 1987.

Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said aerial searches showed the ferry was floating upside down and had not sunk. Rescuers were concentrating search efforts around the overturned ferry, he told reporters.
Distraught relatives wait for news at port

Hundreds of relatives gathered at a command centre in Banjarmasin’s Trisakti port, awaiting word on family members believed to be aboard the ferry. Many anxiously checked passenger manifests and rescue lists as authorities continued searching for survivors.
"I was shocked when I saw my uncle’s name on the passenger list," said a woman who goes by a single name, Bunga. "But I felt relieved after officials told me he had been rescued."
Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands where ferries are a common method of travel. Disasters occur regularly, with weak safety enforcement often blamed.

Last month, at least 211 people were rescued from an Indonesian ferry that caught fire in rough seas near the Indonesian tourist island of Bali, while one person was found dead and four others remain missing.
The incident happened less than two weeks after another Indonesian ferry, the Mutiara Sentosa 2, caught fire in waters off the main island of Java, leaving at least five people dead.
Sunday’s accident comes just four days after a fire that gutted a passenger ferry in the Philippines killed at least 76 people, with at least 10 others still missing.

articles.title: ‘Filipiñana’ selected as PH’s official entry to 2027 Oscars
articles.summary: Rafael Manuel's Filipiñana is selected as the country’s official entry to the 2027 Oscars from among eight shortlisted by the Film Academy of the Philippines for the Best International Feature Film…

blocks.text: PASAY CITY, Philippines – Filipiñana is the Philippines’ official entry to the 99th Academy Awards, or the 2027 Oscars, in the Best International Feature Film category, the Film Academy of the Philippines (FAP) announced on Sunday, September 13.

The film, written and directed by Rafael Manuel, beat out seven other contenders shortlisted by FAP: Carl Joseph Papa’s 58th, Jade Castro’s All the Things I Leave You, Sigrid Andrea P. Bernardo’s I’mPerfect, Raymond Red’s Manila’s Finest, Jerrold Tarog’s Quezon, Lawrence Fajardo’s Silenced Nights, and Jun Robles Lana’s Sisa.
“All the eight films, each one of them has the potential to tell the Filipino story in a global manner,” said FAP director general Paolo Villaluna at a press conference.

As defined by the Oscars, an international film is a feature-length motion picture, over 40 minutes long, produced outside the United States and its territories with a predominantly non-English dialogue track, meaning more than 50% of the dialogue is in languages other than English. Animated and documentary feature films are also permitted.

According to Deadline, the deadline for Best International Feature Film submissions is on September 30, with the Oscars set to reveal the official shortlist of 15 films on December 15. The final nominees will be announced on January 21, 2027.
The next Oscars will be held on March 14, 2027 at the Dolby Theater in Los Angeles.
Filipiñana’s recognition stems from its portrayal of Philippine society and American colonialism. The film depicts postcolonial divisions, labor, and social inequality in the country.
“Different voices, new ways of storytelling, new forms, that’s what we want [to resonate],” said Filipiñana producer Bianca Balbuena.

Originally made as a short film that won the Silver Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival in 2020, Filipiñana tells the story of Isabel, who works as a tee girl at a country club’s golf course. It is a coming-of-age story that explores wealth and poverty in Philippine society.
In February, Filipiñana — which runs for 100 minutes — bagged a Special Jury Award at the prestigious Sundance Film Festival.
Aside from Filipiñana, FAP supports 58th and Agapito for Oscars consideration in the Best Documentary Feature Film and Best Live Action Short Film categories, respectively.
“I hope all eyes are in the Philippines now, all Hollywood eyes. I think we have a good chance with the three titles here,” Villaluna said.
“I hope the Filipinos support all our films,” Villaluna added. “We are the masters of cinema, we are good storytellers.”
At the previous Oscars, Lav Diaz’s Magellan earned the nod as the Philippines’ official entry for the Best International Feature Film category. – Angel Camille Dio/Rappler.com
Angel Camille Dio is a Rappler intern studying BA Journalism at Polytechnic University of the Philippines.
